If you don't already have the battered key, head to the building south-west of Seers' Village Bank, and search the north-east bookcase to get a slashed book and a battered key. Enter the north building with the anvil icon, and let yourself in to the workshop the same way as in the Elemental Workshop I quest.
Next, go into the northern water elemental room and search the machinery to the south-west side of the room. You will receive the key used to unlock the hatch in the main room.
Note: If you do not read the scroll, you will not get the search option for the machinery.

Note: Before you go down, quickly "mine" two elemental ores (three if you desire a mind shield) from the west room, and smelt them into elemental metals in the south room (you will need 4 coal per elemental bar). Ironmen may find coal at the mine west of Seers' Village; 20 Agility is required to access it through a shortcut.

Go to the middle of the room and use the key on the locked hatch. Once you're downstairs, you need to fix the machinery. First, go to the "Schematic crate" (directly beside an old lever) to the south and take both the crane and the lever schematics. Then go back upstairs and use one of your bars on the workbench (make sure you only make one in the smithing menu, as the default will be make all!) and make the crane claw. Do not make a helmet yet!
Now, go back down and pull the south-western lever right next to the old crane, and then use the claw on the crane.

Next, head up the small stairs to your west (not up the hatch, but onto the metal construct) to get to the upper level. Open the junction box in the west to work on the pipes for the press (click on the ends you want to connect). You'll want to arrange them as seen on the left.

Hint: The player is led to assume that the machine operates by steam pressure. There is a huge entry pipe that leads from outside the workshop, suggesting that this is a power input source. Observe the lever schematic and the relative pipe entry points. The lever schematic indicates that it is in the middle position normally, blocking flow from the middle pipe, and requires pulling to either side to activate and allow flow from the middle pipe to the outer pipes.

Explanation of the solution: The correct solution is worked out from the clue given by the lever schematic as well as by seeing how the 6 pipes are connected to the back of the junction box. These correspond to the pipe ends in the interface. The lever schematic shows that the middle pipe coming from the lever, top-right in the interface, allows steam to flow towards the lever and must therefore be connected to the large supply pipe, top-middle in the interface. Next, the 2 remaining pipes coming from the lever, bottom-right and bottom-middle in the interface, must be connected to the 2 pipes coming from the press, top-left and bottom-left in the interface. The only combination that works is bottom-right to top-left and bottom-middle to bottom-left.

For the next two parts, you'll need to search some crates in the bottom and upstairs area. The small cog, medium cog, large cog and piece of pipe are located randomly in crates for each player. However, only certain crates contain items: on the bottom floor try searching the double-stacked crates next to the large exit staircase, the single crate north-west by the stairwell down, the double-stacked crate east of the west water valve, the double-stacked crates south-east, and the crate next to the schematics crate. Upstairs try searching the double-stacked crate south-east above the old crane and the double-stacked crate directly north-west of the junction box. If searching a crate does not yield an "It's empty." message or produce an item, it is not possible to find an item within. Once you have found all 3 cogs and the piece of pipe, you can stop searching the crates. If you lose one of the items before using it you can retrieve it in the same crate it was found previously.

Use the pipe on the broken pipe upstairs on the northernmost point of the scaffolding. Then for the cogs, take them back down the steps to the wind tunnel on the east side of the track. On the side of the wind tunnel are three pins (under 2 yellow directional arrows). By using the cogs on the machine pins, you want to stick the small one on the upper-left pin, the medium one on the lower left, and the large one on the right.
Place your elemental metal on the jig cart, which should be on the south crane right now. (If it is not, you must have already pulled the lever with the [[Mine cart sign
The crane

The west lever (near the crane) will raise and lower the crane, and the east one (also near the crane) will rotate the crane. Raise the crane, rotate it, lower it to dip it into the lava and raise it back out. The bar should now be glowing orange.
Rotate the crane back, lower it and raise it again to deposit the bar on the jig.
Note: Make sure to lower the crane and then raise it again in order to correctly deposit the bar. Not doing so will cause the bar to remain on the crane.
Pull the lever right behind you, by the yellow sign (north of the crane) to move the cart to the next station. Remember this lever, you will need to use it to move the cart after each step.
Go to where the cart now is and pull the lever to the east, north-west of the yellow sign. The bar will be flattened by a steam press.
Go back to the yellow-sign lever and move the cart forward again.
If you haven't already fixed the pipe, go upstairs (not up the hatch, but onto the metal construct), and use the [[pipe (Elemental Workshop II)
The water tank
You will see an old lever, a corkscrew lever, and two [[Water valve (Elemental Workshop)
Pull the old lever to open the door, then turn the corkscrew lever twice to pull the cart into the tank. Close the door again with the old lever.

Make sure the eastern valve is closed, then open up the western valve (between two stacks of crates). The bar should turn blue once it gets cooled by the water. If it does not, the eastern valve is open.
Close the western valve again, then open the eastern one to let the water out and close it down again.
Note: If the eastern valve reports that it is sucking air, you skipped step 6 (Fixing the pipe).

Open the door with the old lever, turn the corkscrew twice to deposit the cart back on the track, close the door again using the old lever. The cart will not move forward again while the door is open.
Pull the yellow-sign lever again to move the cart to the next station.
Turn on the [[fan blade
Note: If the fan reports that it is sucking air , the cogs are not correct.
Pull old lever to turn off fan or cart will not move forward in the next step.
Go back and pull the lever to advance the cart again.
Pick up the primed bar!
Do this twice if you want the shield.

Go down one more level to where there are two doors, one with the mind symbol and the other with the body symbol. Go into the mind room (nearest), and place your bar on the extractor gun and operate the extractor hat next to it. A part of you will be drained into the bar turning it into a primed mind bar (that will be picked upstairs in the old crane).
This will temporarily lower your Magic level by 20.

NOTE: You can power multiple bars while here, but each additional bar will drain your Magic by another 20 levels. Power an additional bar if you wish to make a mind shield at the same time as your mind helmet (this is not required to complete the quest).

Once you have picked up the bar/s from the extractor gun, go back up to the workshop. The beaten book is required to be in your inventory to make the mind helmet, otherwise you will make a mind shield. Make a mind helmet out of the bar and the quest is complete.
Congratulations, quest complete!

After the quest is completed, if you have gathered an additional powered bar, make the mind shield with the slashed book in your inventory. Using a bar on the anvil with the slashed book in your inventory will make a mind shield, otherwise you will make a second mind helmet.
Both the mind shield and helmet can be sold on the grand exchange for Mind shield coins and Mind helmet coins respectively.
Talk to Lazim north-east of the quarry. (Of course! → Okay, I'll get on with it.)
Bring him 32 kg of sandstone, it doesn't have to be all at once. You can break down big pieces with a chisel.
Use your chisel on the sandstone (32 kg).
Place the base on the flat ground.
Repeat the process for a 20 kg body.
Use your chisel on the statue.
Talk to Lazim and pick any head (remember which head you picked).
Mine two 5 kg pieces of granite (not sandstone!). (Ironmen: Mine a 3rd piece of any size for King's Ransom)
Make the head you chose (if you don't make the head you chose, you will have to make another head). The other 5 kg granite piece is used later.
If you did not bring clay or coal, mine some now.
Talk to him and you'll fall into a temple.
Talk to Lazim.
If you climb up the ladder and up the sand pile next to the statue now, you'll be able to exit and enter the temple from any outer room on the bottom floor later.
Use your chisel on the fallen statue four times to get all its limbs.
Talk to Lazim again to retrieve the statue head.
Take-sigil from the pedestal south of Lazim to get the M sigil.
Skip this step and come back after the next if you have no inventory space.
Go around all the rooms through the outer hallways and pick up the R, K and Z sigils. The matching limbs are automatically used and consumed to open the doors.
Go to the centre room after collecting all four sigils
Try to open the doors to place the sigils. Make sure to complete each dialogue.
Climb the ladder.
Use soft clay on the pedestal. (Cast a fire spell on the frozen fountain if you still need a water source.)
Use a chisel on the 5 kg granite.
Place the new stone head in the pedestal. The original head will be slightly too small. The new head should fit perfectly and trigger a cutscene (Make sure to finish dialogue).

North-west: use your bread or cake or pie on Pentyn. You may have to right-click again on Pentyn to make sure you are using the food on him and not on the magic spell. (It's okay, I don't need any help.)
North-east: cast wind bolt, blast, wave, or surge on the [[furnace (Enakhra's Lament)
South-east: light the 6 [[brazier (Enakhra's Lament)
South-west: cast fire bolt, blast, wave, or surge on the [[crust of ice
Pass through the magic barrier and climb the ladder. (If you can't pass through barrier, talk to Lazim)
Cast crumble undead on the boneguard.
Climb down the stone ladder to the south.
Turn on Protect from Melee and talk to the new boneguard. (Of course, I'll help you out. → Okay, I'll start building.)
Take 3 sandstones from the [[rubble (Enakhra's Lament)
Use a sandstone on the southern wall, then use your chisel on the wall. Repeat to completion.
Talk to the boneguard again.
Congratulations, quest complete!
Medium Desert Diary
A pickaxe, chisel.

You can start this quest by speaking with Lazim, who is located just south of the Bandit Camp and west of the Ancient Pyramid. The simplest way of getting there is to travel with the free ferry south-west of Al Kharid to the Ruins of Unkah and run north from there. Alternatively, if you have a Pharaoh's Sceptre you can teleport to Jaldraocht (the Ancient Pyramid) and run west. Have at least four free inventory spaces at the start of the quest. You need to buy a Shantay Pass (5 coins) from the guard to exit the Ruins of Unkah and may need more if you come back to buy water from him.

Lazim introduces himself as a down-on-his-luck sculptor who once made statues for royalty but has been unable to hold a chisel since an unspecified accident. He wants your help building a statue to decorate the desolate area. Agree to help him. He will ask you to gather 32 kilograms' worth of sandstone from the nearby quarry.

There are four sizes of sandstone: 1 kg, 2 kg, 5 kg, and 10 kg. You can use your chisel on big blocks to make them smaller, if necessary. At a higher Mining level, you'll get bigger blocks. Speak to Lazim and tell him you have the sandstone once you have finished. You will have to give the pieces to him one by one, eliciting some caustic remarks.

After you've given Lazim exactly 32 kg, he will attach them with magic to make a 32kg sandstone block. Use your chisel on the block that he gives you to make a sandstone base. Talk to him again and then use it on the flat ground next to him.

You now need 20 kilograms of sandstone for the body. After you've given him the required amount and he gives you the 20kg sandstone block, use your chisel on it to make a sandstone body and then attach it to the base. Lazim will grow increasingly angrier with your performance. He seems to be still missing something and tells you to chisel the statue a bit more. Talk to him again; he seems impatient, expecting something to have happened. He decides the statue is only missing a head, to be made out of granite from the same quarry. He lets you decide whose head the statue should bear. (If you want, you can tell him about the events of The Giant Dwarf if you have completed that quest; he will not allow you to use the head of your chosen company director because you no longer remember how it looks.)

You now have to choose the head of the statue. You may choose between either your own head (which he will not allow either), Lazim's head, a camel's head, or a god's head, with the choice of Zamorak or Icthlarin. Mine a 5 kg piece of granite (not sandstone!). Chisel it into a head (if you sculpt the wrong head, Lazim will insult you but allow you to change your choice at the cost of the granite) and keep the other in your inventory for later in the quest. In order to save time later, mine a second 5kg piece of granite and some clay as well. There is a general store at the Bandit Camp where you can buy a bucket of water to use on the clay to make it soft (The empty buckets can be given to Drew). Also mine a piece of coal if you don't have one already, as you will need it later.
Note: Mining granite is a Hard Desert Diary task.

Use the head on the statue. It will fall through the ground, creating a large hole. As you peer into it, Lazim pushes you inside. You hurt your duodenum and appear in an ancient temple below next to the sculptor and broken statue. Talk to Lazim, who says everything has gone according to plan. You deduce that he is not in fact a sculptor but promises you a share of whatever treasure you find in the temple if you help him. He explains you have fallen to the bottom floor and need to make your way to the top. The doors in the temple do not require keys but stone limbs instead; he suggests you mine or chisel them off the statue.
Note: If you teleport away at this point, you will need to re-enter the temple via the south-western secret entrance.

full.h: The Camel, the Witch, and the Prison

steps.t: Use your chisel or pickaxe on the statue to get a stone left arm, stone right arm, stone left leg, and stone right leg, which you'll use as keys to unlock the doors to the rooms. Lazim also returns the stone head to you, which had fallen off the statue. Should you need to exit the temple, the ladder next to the statue's remains leads to a pile of sand you can climb to the surface. This will unlock this entrance permanently.

Go around the outside track to each of the rooms through the doors, as the door in the western corridor is locked. Each door requires one of the limbs. Opening a door will give you a headache and trigger a cutscene. You should travel anticlockwise for the cut scenes to be in the correct order and collect the sigils from the pedestals as you go. The first shows a mysterious woman called Enakhra cheering at the completion of the temple for her lord. The second, four Knights of Avarrocka come to destroy the sorceress and her temple, only to be slain effortlessly by Enakhra's magic. One knight is left alive, frozen in ice. In the third cutscene, a camel-headed man named Akthanakos apparently convinces Enakhra to defect from Zamorak, for whom the temple is but who would rather have a weapon, to 'their side'. She pretends to agree, upon which the man leaves. In the next cutscene, she is shown animating bones to a weak skeleton in an attempt to create a weapon for Zamorak and is not satisfied.

As you pass the bigger rooms along the way, take the Z sigil, R sigil, and K sigil, which together with the M sigil in the room in which you started, make up the consonants of 'Zamorak'. You may also want to climb the ladders and sandpiles to unlock all four secret entrances. After you've unlocked all of the outer doors with the four limbs, go towards the middle and use the sigil to unlock the door. You may also unlock the other three doors. (This will permanently remove the sigils.)

Go up the ladder. A magic barrier is blocking your progress and there is a curious pedestal next to the ladder. Go back to Lazim and ask him about it. He asks whether there is a recess in it, which you confirm. He suggests placing the statue head into it. Try doing so; it will fit, but not perfectly. If you return to Lazim for advice, he says you should make a mould of the recess somehow and use that as a template to make another head from granite. If you did not bring soft clay, regular clay can be mined in the quarry. Take the ladder next to Lazim up and climb up the sand pile to resurface. There is a general store to the north where you can purchase a bucket, bowl or jug with water and use it on the clay to make soft clay. When you return, climb down the secret entrance a few tiles east of the hole you fell down to get back into the temple.

Use soft clay on the pedestal to make a positive camel head mould and then use the chisel on a piece of medium-sized granite (5 kg) to make a new stone head. Place this granite camel head into the pedestal to be greeted by another cutscene. It shows Akthanakos standing by the pedestal, confused. Enakhra reveals her betrayal and freezes him, expressing her loyalty to Zamorak.
Optional: Use a second soft clay on the granite head on the pedestal to make a camel mask for yourself, but only after you've crafted and placed in the new stone head.

A pickaxe or chisel, runes for [[fire bolt

Lazim will appear next to you after the cutscene, complimenting you on opening the doors. He explains the magic barrier will not let you through but it may open if you solve each of the four puzzles in the surrounding rooms. You will know you have succeeded because the corresponding globes on the pedestal will be lit. You may wish to start with the blood room, as it will unlock advice about the other ones.
Take the north-east corridor and examine the furnace. Its grate is blocked and requires a strong blast of air to clear. Use a wind spell, bolt or stronger, on the furnace to clear out the room.
Warning: Standing too long in this room without lighting any braziers will do damage due to darkness! Light the candle before entering the room to avoid damage.

Take the south-east corridor and investigate each braziers to see what kind of fire used to burn there. The appropriate Firemaking level is required to see what item goes into what brazier, but it is not required to actually add the items to the brazier, meaning that you can simply guess and check to figure out which item goes into which brazier without needing the Firemaking level. The items are: logs, oak logs, willow logs, maple logs, a candle, and coal. Use the appropriate items on the braziers to light them.

Take the north-west corridor and talk to the old knight Pentyn, frozen by a magical spell. He believes you are a shapeshifting Mahjarrat there to torture him again. He explains he is a Knight of Avarrocka and has been frozen, wounded and hungry for many years. Give him your bread, pie, cake, pizza, or baked potato with toppings. He will not accept half-eaten food. Make sure to right-click and use it on him, rather than left-click to eat. You may have to right-click again on Pentyn to make sure you are using the food on him and not on the magic spell.

He will reminisce about one of his family members, with the specific one depending on what type of food was given to him, and thank you for the memory. He'll still be stuck, but will no longer be in hunger.

He will also offer advice on the other rooms. The frozen fountain did not yield to fire nor swords and is likely magical in nature. The furnace produces choking fumes and requires a good breeze to clear. The fires in the dark room will have gone out since he last saw them and require relighting.
Take the south-west corridor to find a frozen fountain that will require more than a regular fire to thaw. Cast a fire spell, bolt or stronger, on the frozen fountain to thaw it.

A chisel and runes for crumble undead

After all four globes are lit, speak to Lazim again, who will warn you of traps beyond the barrier, such as giant skeletons that will rend your limbs from your body. Go north through the barrier and up the ladder. You will indeed encounter a Boneguard south of the ladder. Talk to it. It warns you that you will not pass it unless it 'crumbles to dust' and attack if you don't run away in time. Cast Crumble Undead on it. Your spell must hit the guard. The boneguard collapses and a freed spirit thanks you. It asks you to please bury the five big bones it has left behind.

Pass the boneguard's remains and climb down the ladder. You'll see another boneguard. If you want, you may also climb down the ladder from the other side, where Enakhra herself is standing. She angrily tells you not to interrupt her concentration and fires two spells at the Boneguard opposite her to prevent him from escaping before Zamorak can collect it, his weapon. Speak to the Boneguard. It will attack you once, stating that someone so easy to hit is not worth its time.

This time, turn on Protect from Melee and talk to it. It will try to attack you a couple of times — then, it will be impressed and ask for your help. It will tell you that it was put under Enakhra's control millennia ago and that she had tricked him into this state of slavery. When her concentration wavered, the Boneguard managed to construct part of a wall to obscure Enakhra's line of sight, but her spells have strengthened lately. Agree to help the Boneguard by finishing the wall so that it can be free. It promises you its amulet as a reward in return. It tells you to take stones from the nearby pile of rubble, stack them on the unfinished wall, trimming them with a chisel so they fit and that it will require but three loads.

If you want, you may quiz him for more backstory on himself and Enakhra. He says the latter is a 'coward and a despicable traitor' who supported Zamorak when he became a god. She built him this temple as a gift, but he did not care and she has been hidden inside ever since. He himself was once a proud mage but has long been trapped in Boneguard form, forced to defend Enakhra's temple from intruders when he believed her lies about wanting to become allies and end their rivarly.

Take three pieces of sandstone from the pile of bricks, use the sandstone on the wall and then use your chisel on the wall to trim it. Once you've built the wall, Enakhra will be furious with you. Optionally, cross to the other side to talk to her. She will say the Boneguard, Akthanakos, is much harder to control now and that he supports someone whose name should not be mentioned. She also scolds you for dishonouring Zamorak's name.

Talk to the boneguard. It will thank you, crumble and reveal itself to be another Mahjarrat, the camel-headed Akthanakos. He is free from slavery after thousands of years and gives you his amulet in thanks. It allows you to understand camels and Ugthanki as well as containing teleports back to the temple. He then confronts his rival in a cutscene.

Enakhra blows up the wall and faces her nemesis. Akthanakos laughs and says Lord Zaros will be happy to aid him should, as Enakhra announces, Zamorak come to punish him for destroying his weapon. They transform into their skeleton forms and announce they will fight in the North before teleporting away.

A bowl spawns in the house east of Auguste on the

Note: This quest can be completed in two trips to Entrana if bank space is managed well. Follow the guidance in each section to see what items are needed and when to return to a bank.
Travel to Entrana while obeying its inventory rules and carrying only the items required for this section. Talk to Auguste, found on the western side of the island, just north of the Herblore shop.

Note: If boosting the requirements, you must boost them all before talking to Auguste. Once the quest is started, there will be a further skill check of 36 Crafting to add the unlit candle to the origami balloon, and 20 Firemaking to fly the balloon.

Auguste will ask for your help in testing his balloon system. After he shows the player his new design, talk to him again and he will request that you bring a number of items to create some test balloons.
Use the papyrus on the ball of wool to create a balloon structure, then use the unlit candle on it to create an origami balloon. Do not light the balloon or else you will have to get the items again!

Talk to Auguste to see a short cutscene of the balloon launch. After that, talk to him again, and he will take the remaining two pieces of papyrus and the sack of potatoes from you. In a second cutscene, the player launches the next balloon, which is attacked by an angry mob of peasants.
Finally, Auguste will ask the player to get the materials for a real balloon, as well as give you a basket of apples and Auguste's sapling.
Use the empty sacks on the sand pit to the south of Auguste to create 8 sandbags, then talk to him again to give him all of the remaining items you have brought with you.
Note: All of the chat options for giving him items should be used, so if there are some remaining you may have forgotten to bring an item with you.

Once you have given him all of the items in the previous section, you will need to retrieve the remaining required items. You may consider banking in Pest Control, either using Minigame Teleport or returning to Port Sarim and travelling there and back via the ships.

Note: If you plan to grow Auguste's sapling instead of buying the willow branches on the Grand Exchange, plant the sapling in any tree patch and give the local farmer the basket of apples to look after it. Once it is fully grown, check its health, wait a half hour, then cut willow branches from it by using secateurs on the tree. You can only get 6 branches at once, so you'll need to wait another half hour to get all 12.
Return to Entrana and use a willow branch on the balloon basket to start a cutscene. Once it concludes, the log storage will appear. If you brought additional noted logs, you may store them now.

Talk to Auguste again. He'll describe some of what the player should notice and some tips on how to fly the balloon. An interface to control the balloon will appear. Manoeuvre through the obstacle course without hitting anything (including birds, trees, houses, and clouds) and safely land on the well-marked landing spot on the third screen. See the sections below for an easy route to complete the flight.
Clicking any control advances the balloon one "space" to the right.
The top button (drop sandbag) moves the balloon two spaces up (UP 2).
The next button (use log) moves the balloon one space up (UP 1).
"Relax" advances the balloon to the right without changing altitude (RIGHT).
The normal rope lowers the balloon by one space (DOWN 1),
The red rope lowers the balloon by two spaces (DOWN 2).
Clicking "Bail" will cancel the flight.

The numbers at the side of sack and log buttons correspond to how many times player can use the resources respectively; therefore, fuel is limited. If the player runs out of fuel, they can still "relax" or lower altitude (by pulling ropes).

A tip is that how the balloon appears to travel is not as important as where it will end up. If the balloon meets a cloud right above it and a bird in front of it, it is possible to go right through both obstacles by dropping sacks or pulling the red rope (raising and dropping the balloon by 2 spaces respectively). The balloon will fly high or low enough to avoid the bird, and will advance one space forward to avoid the cloud. It might not seem like the balloon can fit through, but it can.

There will be three screens to navigate across. The balloon should end up one space above the landing pad, with no air space in between. Flying past the landing pad would get the balloon blown away, and getting the balloon in the space with the landing pad would cause it to smash to the ground—in both cases, the flight would be considered unsuccessful. The player needs to restart the flight by preparing the logs and tinderbox again before going to Entrana, although they don't have to rebuild the balloon.

After the balloon has landed, talk to Auguste to finish the quest. If you wish to unlock additional routes, talk to him after the quest to open the interface and choose the route you wish to unlock.

Talk to Veronica standing just outside the courtyard of the Draynor Manor. She wants you to find her fiancé, Ernest, who had gone to the manor an hour ago for directions and has not come back yet.

Make your way to the Grand Museum in Civitas illa Fortis. Inspect the empty display to start the quest, then speak to Curator Herminius; fed up with how long the guards are taking, he will take the investigation into his own hands, and ask you to see if there's anything he missed.

Investigate the set of tools on the ground behind the display to find out they are specialist tools, and inspect the display again to observe that the glass was tampered with. Next, talk to the nearby citizens, academics, and tourists around the floor and ask whether they had seen anything suspicious. The person who gives you the information is random for each player, but one will eventually mention a shifty individual skulking around who left through the front door and turned right towards the landing site.

Speak to Regulus Cento at the Civitas landing site (not in Varrock) and ask whether he's seen anybody suspicious around. He'll mention a person carrying a case who wanted to have a go with his bird. However, Regulus refused, and the person went east to the Fortis Cothon instead. Make sure you have one free inventory space, and then head to the Cothon and talk to any Trader Crewmember. Ask them about the man with the case, and they will ask for a small favour in exchange for the information. Agree, and they'll give you some tattered sails which need to be fixed up at Artima's Crafting Supplies.

Head just south of the Cothon, to the shop marked on the map with a , and speak with Artima. Tell her you were hoping for some help, and she will ask you for a favour as well; to thank the crew for bringing in her latest shipment. She will then give you the repaired sails. Use the sails on any trader crewmember, and they'll tell you a "grey-haired fella" came by and asked if he could have a go with their boat. The crew then explained to him how to charter a ship properly, and sailed the man to Port Sarim.

Make your way to Port Sarim by any method you wish, such as the charter ship, the Rat Pits Minigame Teleport, or a planted spirit tree. Once there, head all the way to the southernmost dock and speak any trader crewmember about the grey-haired man. They will tell you that he wandered up north in search of some runes to get a hold of.

The nearest rune store is Betty's Magic Emporium, found in the north-west corner of Port Sarim. With one free inventory space, make your way to the store and ask Betty about the man. Betty will mention that he wore a monocle, and that he didn't know what he was looking for when he arrived. She'll give you some notes she took while trying to understand him, hoping you'll make sense of them.

Based on the notes, the runes being requested are those for casting Varrock Teleport. With all this in mind, the man who best fits the description you have been given so far is in fact Haig Halen, the curator of the Varrock Museum. Make your way there, and tell him that you're looking for Xerna's Diadem; he will immediately act suspicious, claiming that he can't help you. You may now destroy the notes, leaving an open inventory space for the next section of the quest.

Pickpocket the curator to receive a storeroom key, and use it to enter the storeroom to the north-east of the museum (right under the stairs to the first floor). Search the single unstacked crate in the middle of the room to discover that Xerna's Diadem is hidden inside, along with various other artefacts that don't seem to belong there.

Return to Curator Haig Halen, and speak to him to begin an interrogation in which you press him for answers. A "Shame-o-meter" will appear on the screen; you must now select chat options that will shame him. The exact sequence varies for each player, but the most effective options are usually calling him a thief or disparaging his museum as being full of stolen goods. Use the table below to find options which increase shame, and avoid options which decrease shame.

Once the shame meter reaches 100%, Haig will explain what happened. Haig will claim that, during his visit to the Grand Museum, he saw a thief break in and steal Xerna's Diadem. Haig will then claims that he used the combat skills he picked up during his time in the Varrock Guard to subdue the thief. However, stuck on what to do next, Haig explains that he decided to take the artefact back to Varrock Museum for "safekeeping."

The player offers to omit the details of the theft to the Grand Museum, as long as Haig arranges the safe return of the diadem. After Haig agrees to return it, head back to Civitas illa Fortis (you may choose to take a free flight from Primio to the south-east) and speak with Curator Herminius at the Grand Museum to complete the quest.

Crush your mud rune with the pestle and mortar, and then use it on the bucket of sap to create magic glue. Repair the machine using your maple logs, oak logs and the glue. You will need to have a hammer and a saw in your inventory.

If you did not bring a bucket of sap ahead of time, there is a tree just north of Brimstail's cave, between two Oak trees, that you can extract sap from. Use a knife on it with a bucket in your inventory to extract the sap.

Now, you will have to unlock and restart the machine. For this, you will need more crystal discs—talk to Brimstail to get some from him. You can talk to him multiple times to get more shapes. If you can no longer get discs from Brimstail, drop the discs and talk to him again to get more discs. Alternatively, you can exchange the discs at the exchanger next to the machine.
To work this machine, you have to fit crystal discs to the numbers shown. The numbers will be different for everybody; therefore, you have to solve this mostly yourself. This is how it works:
To the west side is a chart showing the values of each colour.
The crystal is equal to:
Red: 1
Orange: 2
Yellow: 3
Green: 4
Blue: 5
Indigo: 6
Violet: 7
This value is multiplied by the number of sides each crystal has:
Circle has 1 side.
Triangle has 3 sides.
Square has 4 sides.
Pentagon has 5 sides.
Example 1: a 4 can be a red square or a green circle (1 * 4)
Example 2: a 7 can only be a violet circle (7 * 1)
Example 3: a 12 can be a green triangle or a yellow square (4 * 3)
Some of the colours can be easily mixed up, since they are very similar (e.g. blue, indigo, and violet). Hover them with your mouse to be sure.

The yellow circle can never be obtained. If the puzzle requires a value of three, you must use the red triangle instead. Brimstail cannot directly give you any circles, or red coloured shapes. If you need the lower value shapes the exchanger must be used.

There is a token exchanger on the right-hand side, which allows you to insert various tokens and change them for others of the same value. You cannot exchange more than 35 points worth at a time, but you may exchange a single token for many other lower valued tokens if its value is high enough. You will always receive the same value back, in different tokens. For example, if you need an indigo pentagon (30), and have a violet pentagon (35). Put the violet pentagon into the exchanger, and keep declining the transaction until the machine offers you an indigo pentagon (30) and a red pentagon (5).

To unlock the machine, you have to create a single disc worth the number of points shown on Oaknock's machine. The numbers are different for everyone. As a general strategy, try and get the smaller numbers and it's easier. Any violet pentagons or similar if not needed may be exchanged for ones of a lower value using the Oaknock's exchanger.

Once unlocked, you need to restart the machine. For this, you will need to fit six separate tokens to three different numbers (1 for the first number, 2 for the second and 3 for the third). Be patient—it can take a while to get all the tokens that you need. You may speak to Brimstail to get more tokens which may make getting the ones you want easier; it is possible to solve the puzzle by continuously asking for and dropping coins until you get the ones you need.

An example of a completed machine. Note: You must fill all slots to unlock the machine! In this example, using two violet triangles turned the light green, but still did not work. If this happens, you can just use the exchanger to turn it into two pieces, since the total points stay the same.

Once you have unlocked the machine, speak to Brimstail again. The once cute creatures are revealed to be evil creatures. After the cut-scene, talk to Brimstail and he will tell you to speak to King Narnode.
There are six creatures in total, and they have 1 Hitpoint each.
1 - One by Brimstail (he may kill it for you).
2 - One by King Narnode. (You may need to [[Ranged
range]] or mage this one, as it can get stuck behind the trapdoor.)
3 - One at the top of the Grand Tree, by the prison. (Do not climb down the ladders immediately after killing the creature—it will not count as a kill.)
4 - One by the giant tortoises in the pen north-west of the Grand Tree (north of the toad swamp).
5 - One by the Gnome Stronghold Spirit Tree.
6 - One by the entrance to the Gnome Stronghold. Go south from the Grand Tree, down the ramp and keep walking to the main entrance of the Stronghold.
Note: If Brimstail kills the evil creature, or if you mess up a creature kill count at any time, the last Evil Creature will spawn at the entrance to Gnome Stronghold.

Head to the Draynor Village marketplace and ask Martin the Master Gardener nearby if there is anything you can help with. He will mention that his roses haven't been doing as well as they used to. He suspects something's wrong, and wants you to ask several other members of the G.A.G. (Group of Advanced Gardeners) if they're having the same problems as him.
You will have to speak with any five members of the Group of Advanced Gardeners. These are the gardeners that tend farming patches around Gielinor.

Note: All farmers added since the launch of Old School RuneScape do not count, including: Ayesha in Al Kharid, Lammy Langle north-east of the Woodcutting Guild, Imiago in Tai Bwo Wannai, and Marisi in Hosidius. You can ask them why the crops are failing, but they will only respond by saying they do not know anything about that.
Some of the easiest to reach are:

The "Fairy Godfather" has replaced the queen; ask where she is and he'll tell you that the queen has fallen to some sort of illness and is currently under the care of Fairy Nuff. She'll give you details about the queen's illness and give you a symptoms list to take to a wizard named Zandar Horfyre, in the Dark Wizards' Tower.

Travel to Falador and head west to reach the Dark Wizards' Tower. Climb up to the top floor and talk to Zandar, who will take the symptom list and then suggest talking to Malignius Mortifer about killing the Tanglefoot. This necromancer can be found on the crossroads south of Falador. You can fast travel to him with a skills necklace (to the Crafting Guild).

He'll tell you he could probably help, but wants something from you first. He wants a skull from a grave in the Draynor Manor backyard. Head to the back of the manor and dig up the grave there. In case you have no spade, there is one inside the manor. If you have dug up the skull previously, you will not find it, and your character will mention that they think they stored it in the bank.
secateurs and the amulet of ghostspeak

Return to Malignius with the skull, who will mention that the queen's illness is the result of an evil creature called the Tanglefoot, and the only way to defeat it is by creating a pair of enchanted secateurs. You will need to take a pair of secateurs and three randomised items to the Nature Grotto in order to bless them. Check your quest log to see what randomised items you need to bring. The list below details how to obtain your items; you may use any method. Once you have them, grab your amulet of ghostspeak and secateurs and travel to the Nature Spirit in the Mort Myre Swamp. He'll bless your secateurs, which will then glow green and turn into the magic secateurs.

Warning: If travelling through the swamp to reach the Nature Grotto, the ghasts may rot the edible seaweed, jangerberries, king worm or lime from the list. If any of these are a required item, bring multiples or a filled druid pouch to avoid losing them.
Note: The randomization will always generate three items in sequence within this ordered list. For example, items #1/#2/#3, items #2/#3#/#4, etc.
magic secateurs

Head back to Zanaris with your magic secateurs. It is highly recommended to bank your Dramen staff at the Zanaris bank before the following fight, as you will need to obtain another one to return if you die here.

From the entrance to the city, travel south-west, past the agility shortcuts, to the mysterious ruins of the Cosmic Altar. Climb through the gap on the west side of the room, and the Gatekeeper there will allow you to pass. Inside the tunnel are a few baby tanglefootii (level 45). Proceed to the end of the tunnel to stumble upon the level 111 Tanglefoot.

The Tanglefoot may only be damaged with the magic secateurs, and your maximum hit will depend on both your Strength and Farming levels. The Tanglefoot may be flinched to avoid taking damage by standing one tile east of the southern end of the corridor, attacking then returning to the eastern tile until his health bar disappears. Protect from Melee is highly recommended if not flinching.

Tip: If a baby tanglefoot walks onto the player's safespot, those with RuneLite may consider using the Menu Entry Swapper plugin, swapping the Attack option for BOTH baby tanglefoot (there are two kinds) to prevent the player from accidentally attacking them.
Once defeated, the Tanglefoot will drop the Queen's secateurs. Pick up the secateurs and return them to the Fairy Godfather.

Wait 5 minutes (Real World Time) and speak to Martin the Master Gardener again. (Quest. → I suppose I'd better go see what the problem is then.)
Now make your way to Fairy Nuff's grotto, just north of the bank in Zanaris.
Take Nuff's Healing certificate off the floor, right-click it and study it. (If lost, you can obtain another Healing certificate by searching the Potion shelves in Fairy Nuff's grotto.)
Head to the south-west area of Zanaris, read the Rune temple sign just south of the Cosmic Altar.
Talk to the Fairy Godfather in the throne room. (Where is the Fairy Queen? → Where could she have been taken to? → Yes, okay.)
Talk to the Co-ordinator just north of the throne room. (The fairy rings.) You can now use the fairy rings.
Talk to Fairy Fixit near the fairy ring west of the throne room. (Why are you carrying that toolbox?)

Now, equip your Dramen staff, and teleport using the fairy ring in this sequence: air, dlr, djq (You will not go anywhere), ajs - (Note: You can right click configure but you must have the Nuff's certificate in your inventory)
Talk to Fairy Nuff and Fairy Very Wise in the NE corner of the area.
Go back to Zanaris (bks) and pickpocket the Fairy Godfather while he and his henchmen aren't looking.
Go back to the hideout and give the Queen's secateurs to Fairy Nuff. (air, dlr, djq, ajs)
Note: Do not mix the magic essence potion before learning how to make it from the Fairy or it will not revive the Fairy Queen when used on her.
Travel to fairy code CKP. Wait here (2-5 mins) until a star flower has grown then pick it. (You must have Nuff's certificate with you for this to work.)
Travel to fairy code DIR. Kill a gorak and pick up its gorak claws. Goraks can be safespotted using some terrain.
Return to the hideout. (air, dlr, djq, ajs)
Talk to Fairy Nuff.
Now use the star flower on your vial of water and grind the gorak claws to receive gorak claw powder, then use the two items on each other to make a magic essence potion.
RIGHT-CLICK use the magic essence on the queen, laying on the stretcher near Fairy Nuff.
Speak with the Fairy Queen to complete the quest.
Congratulations, quest complete!
Note: Do not pickpocket Martin before you start the quest, or you won't be able to continue for 10 consecutive minutes of in-game time.

To start, talk to Martin the Master Gardener in the Draynor Market. He will tell you to come back once his crops are grown, so wait until your quest menu says his crops have had plenty of time to grow; this takes approximately five and a half minutes of logged in time.

Talk to him again. He informs you rather crossly that there is still something wrong with the crops, not believing your story about fairies and accusing you of creating this problem. Agree to investigate for him.
Dramen staff or Lunar staff

Head south-east into the Lumbridge Swamp, towards the hut. Equip a Dramen or Lunar staff and go into Zanaris, and head toward Fairy Nuff's grotto, just north of the bank. Walk in, and you'll see a short cutscene. On the ground and next to one of the potion shelves is Fairy Nuff's certificate; pick it up. Right click and choose "Study". Studying the certificate reveals its back, which is covered with strange fairy symbols.

Talk to the Fairy chef, south of the bank. She will tell you that she's seen similar inscriptions on a sign near the mysterious ruins — the Cosmic Altar ruins in southern Zanaris, next to the tanglefoot area. Go South of the Altar and click on the wall that says " Read Rune Temple Sign".
You must look at the sign and study the certificate.
The symbols say "Cosmic Rune Altar." If you were to translate it, the back of the certificate reads:

Talk to the Fairy Godfather in the Fairy Queen's throne room located next to the Slayer master. Ask him what happened to the Queen, to which he visibly starts panicking and rushes to say that he will create a search party for her. Ask him both questions, and then agree to return to him once you've found the queen. The Godfather gives you permission to use the fairy rings to locate the queen. He asks you to speak to the Co-ordinator outside the room (North of the Godfather) to learn more about the rings.

After talking to the Co-ordinator and being informed of the vast history of the fairy rings and the queen, head West to the fountains, then South to the fairy ring. Talk to Fairy Fixit near the fairy ring, south of the fountains. After that, use the fairy rings while wielding a Dramen staff (or a Lunar staff if you have partially or fully completed Lunar Diplomacy).
You may now use the fairy rings throughout Gielinor without finishing the quest, if you'd prefer.
See the fairy rings guide for all the possible combinations.

With Nuff's certificate in your inventory, use the fairy ring four times in sequence. You will need to repeat this sequence each time you wish to visit the Fairy Queen's hideout. Once you have correctly done it once, the sequence of four appears as an option at the bottom of the teleports list. After the quest you will no longer need Nuff's certificate, but you will still need to do all four teleports. Nuff's certificate in your inventory must be obtained after you meet the required skill levels to complete the quest.
AIR (Islands: South of Witchaven)
DLR (Islands: Poison Waste south of Isafdar)
DJQ (un-attached code, will not teleport you anywhere)
AJS (Islands: Penguins near Miscellania, or Queen's location)

If you end up in the same spot on any code other than DJQ with your character saying "Wow, fairy magic sure is useful!", it could be because the default click-action for the fairy ring is "Last destination (AIP)". Make sure to right-click and choose "Configure".

If you end up on an island with some penguins, you do not have Nuff's certificate in your inventory. You may also have skipped deciphering the certificate's message or simply missed one code in the sequence. (If you get the message "Maybe you need to investigate further first..", this indicates you correctly input the fairy ring sequence but may have skipped the sign at the Cosmic Altar.)

You should be in the Fairy Queen's new location. Just go up the path, and head to the north-eastern room. Talk to Fairy Nuff and to Fairy Very Wise, who will inform you that the queen is not well because the Godfather has hurt her by not returning her magic secateurs. As her essence is drained, she cannot retaliate without obtaining the secateurs, which you accept to bring back.

Head back to Zanaris, and pickpocket the Fairy Godfather. This requires level 40 Thieving to be completed successfully. If you fail, you will be teleported outside Zanaris. A quick way to get back to Zanaris is the Salve graveyard teleport which will place you a few strides away from the Canifis fairy ring.

Try pickpocketing from behind or the side, and make sure neither of his henchmen are looking directly at you. You should get a golden Queen's secateurs. Also, at this point, you will see orks patrolling Zanaris.
Return to the Fairy Queen's Hideout by using the same four-ring sequence listed above.

Warning: If you prepared the ingredients in advance, make sure you give the secateurs to Fairy Nuff before mixing the magic essence/crushing the gorak claw, or you'll have to get the ingredients all over again!

Back at the fairy hideout, talk to Fairy Nuff, and give her the secateurs. She will use them to rejuvenate the queen, but they do not work completely. Nuff tells you that she needs a certain magic essence potion to replenish the queen's missing life energy. To make the potion, you need to collect some Star flowers and gorak claw powder.
Dramen staff or Lunar staff

Return to the fairy ring and use the code CKP, which transports you to a cosmic plane. Move around for about two minutes whilst the Star flowers grow. You can pass the time by talking to the Cosmic Being who lives there, contemplating the mysteries of the universe.

Pick a star flower when ready (49 Farming needed), and add your harvest to the vial of water (57 Herblore needed—however, if you are boosting, wait until you have the gorak claw powder because you need 57 Herblore to finish the potion).
Dramen or Lunar staff, Nuff's certificate

Return to Zanaris, and withdraw any armour and weapons, along with around 10 pieces of good food. Goraks are very accurate, so take the best melee armour you have. They are aggressive, but luckily, they are not located in a multicombat area, therefore you can only fight one at time. However, by remaining in the fairy ring, they will not be aggressive until they are attacked.
Tips:
Goraks use typeless melee attacks, meaning Protection prayers do not have any effect. However, you may use boosting prayers such as Piety.
The accuracy of the goraks' attacks is calculated by your crush defence, so it is recommended to wear crush-resistant armour such as chainmail.
It is possible to safespot the goraks (see picture). However, their aggression and high max hit may render this difficult, so be extra careful if you are low levelled.

At the Zanaris fairy ring, use the sequence DIR to get to another plane full of goraks. They are level 145 or 149 and occasionally drain stat points. Kill them, eating food when necessary and drink restore potions if needed until you get a gorak claw. To leave, equip your staff of choice and teleport to Zanaris using the right-click option on the fairy ring.
Note: Ensure you have retrieved the Queen's secateurs at this point, otherwise a dose of the magic essence potion will be lost and the queen will not regain consciousness.

Crush the claw with a pestle and mortar to get gorak claw powder. Mix the star flower and gorak claw powder into a vial of water to make a magic essence potion (57 Herblore needed). Return to the Resistance Hideout, use a dose of the magic essence potion on the queen, who finally regains her senses.

As the queen angrily prepares to return to Zanaris and take back her throne, Fairy Very Wise and Fairy Nuff remind her that the Fairy Godfather has thugs and orks at his disposal. His "army" has her easily outclassed, compared to her Majesty's small band of loyalists (many of whom are injured). The queen realises the flaw in the plan, and accepts the advice and allows the Fairy Godfather to remain Zanaris' ruler for the time being.
Congratulations, quest complete!
To begin, sail to Wyrmscraig, found slightly south-west of Charred Island. Be sure not to bring a sloop, as it will not fit in a cave entered later in the quest.
Dock at the island and try to run onto the island, and you will be stopped by Ffion.
Run to Auchrie and speak to Cormac in the centre hut.
Speak to Muriel in the building immediately north-east of Cormac's hut, then run to the closest area marked on the map with the Mining icon.
Search the tent for a pickaxe, hammer, and chisel if needed, then inspect the sunstone monolith.
Mine a piece off the sunstone monolith, and chisel it into a sunstone core. The scrawled notebook may be dropped.
Follow the trail of dust to the south-west tip of the island and investigate the large hat.
Head back to Cormac and speak to him.
Sail into Wyrmscraig Cavern on the south-west side of the island with either a skiff or raft.
Kill the three mountain trolls nearest to Mortimer in the cavern. The area is multicombat, lower levelled players may consider praying Protect from Melee.

Speak to Mortimer again, then follow the path north until you see a golem. ( You may exit the cave, via the western exit from the north path, to mine the rocks to gain access to the agility shortcut for ease of access to the cathedral later)
Investigate the golem, use the sunstone core you mined on the golem, then open the chest inside the room (combination: right, left, down, down).
Use a chisel on (or destroy) the ancient sunstone core to get a key, and climb the stairs.
You must now fight the Mad Angel.
Pray against melee, moving behind the angel when she brings her sword back slowly.
When she launches a spiky ball, run to the spot where it lands to avoid taking heavy damage. It will bounce twice to another spot, run to each.

When she starts charging a blue lightning attack, pray Protect from Magic. This will reduce the damage by 50% normally, but will negate all damage if only activated 4 ticks (2.4s) after the charging begins.

"...!" will indicate she is entering her enraged phase. Special attacks will be performed faster, with her lightning attack in three strikes. The third strike will have a delay of 2 ticks (1.2s) rather than 4.
Search the body after defeating her and read the note, then return to Cormac.
Quest complete!

To begin, sail to Wyrmscraig on a raft or skiff (not a sloop), found slightly south-west of Charred Island. Bring all combat equipment and supplies with you, as you will not be able to bank or teleport to the island until the quest is complete. The closest teleport is to Red Rock using a sailors' amulet or charter ship, which also has a shipwright to recover your boat. Access to Red Rock is unlocked during The Red Reef. Alternatively, the closest mainland port with a shipwright is the Corsair Cove.

Ffion will stop the player when attempting to leave the pier after docking, declaring that outsiders are not welcome on Wyrmscraig. Unable to stop you, he will allow the player to pass after a short conversation.
Run to Auchrie, the only settlement on the island, and speak to Cormac in the centre hut. Players with 58 Agility may take the basalt stepping stone shortcut.

Cormac will mention that a villager named Keenan has gone missing, suggesting the player help search for him if they want to get in the other villagers’ good books. He wants you to first check in with Muriel, Keenan's mother. Speak to her in the building immediately north-east (the building with the map icon) to learn that he went off to the mines to observe the sunstone monolith, convinced there is some secret to be discovered from it.

A pickaxe, hammer, and chisel can be obtained by searching the tent just south of the map icon if you didn't bring them. Inspect the sunstone monolith just north of the tent; you will find a scrawled notebook and a trail of dust leading south. You may optionally read the notebook to learn about Keenan's observations of the monolith, during which he felt like the monolith was watching him somehow.

Mine the monolith for a piece of sunstone, then use the chisel on it to create a sunstone core. Now, follow the trail of dust to the south-west tip of the island, and investigate the large hat on the basalt rock. ()

After observing the cathedral, head back to Cormac and tell him what you found. Cormac will explain that the cathedral is the home of the Mad Angel; according to local superstition, she keeps the islanders safe in exchange for tribute, taking one of their own if they fail to do so. He suggests that you try entering the cathedral from the caverns beneath it.

After speaking to Cormac, board either a skiff or raft and sail into Wyrmscraig Cavern on the south side of the island. The entrance to the cavern can be found by where Keenan's hat was, marked by the map icon.
Upon disembarking, a talking skeleton will usher you over. He wants you to deal with three nearby mountain trolls that have blocked the path with rocks.

The area is multicombat, so low level players may consider praying Protect from Melee. Defeat the three trolls, and the skeleton will call you back over. Talk to him again, and the player will then assist in clearing the rest of the rocks. The skeleton introduces himself as the Slayer Master Mortimer, noting that he has not seen the missing villager. You can now use Mortimer as a Slayer Master.
Tip: If you need lead for building the bank chest, head east from Mortimer, then south to the mine, and mine 4 lead ores before continuing.

When ready, follow the path north past the unaggressive wyrms until you see a broken golem. Inspect the golem with at least one free inventory space to remove the dull stone core; next, use the sunstone core you mined on the golem, and it will power up and allow you to enter the cathedral's basement.

Tip: Before continuing into the basement, players with 54 Agility may consider exiting the cave to the west, then mining the rocks shortcut to the east to unlock a quicker path back to the boss should they die during the fight.
If not interested in the methodology to obtain the following solution, you may skip ahead to the end of this section to view the chest's combination.

Upon attempting to climb up the stairs, you will receive a warning note. Read it to find out that there is a creature in the cathedral that has been sealed off by the orders of an individual named Elessia; you will also be prompted to read the back of the note, which appears to be gibberish at first glance.

A worn journal can be found on the table and be read, stating that Elessia has been ill for some time. Next to the table is a locked chest which the player must open with a combination of directional inputs. To get the combination, the back of the note must first be decrypted. The journal mentions the use of keyword ciphers to secure Ardeaglais, and the capitalised word FAITH on the front of the note provides the keyword.

Unlike the simpler Caesar ciphers used in Treasure Trail Cipher Clues, this cipher is a type of the mono-alphabetic substitution cipher, which works by assigning each letter of the alphabet a corresponding letter to be used in its place in the ciphertext. This kind of cipher cannot be brute-forced, due to the replacement alphabet having possible combinations. It can however be defeated using cryptanalysis techniques such as Frequency analysis, as well as targeted decoding of two or three letter words within the ciphertext.

The keyword variant of this cipher begins by replacing the letters of the alphabet starting with "A" with the letters of the keyword. When every letter of the keyword has been used, the remaining letters in the alphabet follow in their original order. Using the keyword "FAITH" results in the following replacement alphabet:
Using the replacement alphabet to decrypt the back of the note results in the following:Starting with sunrise,
Through to sunset,
And as the moon hangs low,
In the southern sky,
We will watch over her.
The first four lines point to a direction:
Sunrise - East/Right
Sunset - West/Left
Hangs low - Down
Southern sky - Down
Which reveals the combination code Right, Left, Down, Down.

Upon unlocking the chest, you will receive an ancient sunstone core and a golem primer. The book may be read as a guide to golem crafting, but this is not required to progress. Use a chisel on the ancient sunstone core to get a key. Alternatively, you can destroy it without the use of tools. Climb the stairs and prepare for a fight with the Mad Angel.

You must now fight the Mad Angel. She has an inaccurate melee attack, as well as three special attacks detailed below. Pray Protect from Melee, and attack with a fast melee weapon; she is weakest to Crush attacks. Upon reaching 255 Hitpoints (~45%), the Mad Angel will become enraged, denoted by a overhead message. During this phase, special attacks are performed quicker, and she will use all three consecutively at the start of this phase.
Once ready to fight, climb the church pew, which may also be used to escape the fight at any time.

After defeating the angel, inspect the body by the throne, confirming that it belongs to Keenan, and read the final letter. Elessia, who you find out is an Icyene, is revealed to have killed Keenan as a result of her illness and hunger, greatly regretting her actions. Before leaving, she constructed a sunstone golem to protect Wyrmscraig in her place, hoping the island's inhabitants will be skilled enough to refine it. Optionally, you can also read the book Observations, obtained from searching one of the bookcases in the cathedral, which tells of Elessia's history.

Exit the cathedral by searching the lock and solving it. The combination to the lock changes each attempt, so you will have to deduce the current code. A simple way to solve the code is to attempt to unlock it while all tumblers are at 1. If any of the boxes on the right side turn green, leave that tumbler in place, then move every other tumbler up one. Repeat until you solve the code. This may take several attempts.

Players with 54 Agility may now use the rocks shortcut to the south-east to return to Auchrie. The rocks must be mined the first time the shortcut is used. An iron pickaxe spawns in Wyrmscraig Cavern for players who forgot to bring one, which can be accessed through the south-west dungeon entrance. Players without 54 Agility can also use the entrance to return to their boat.
Return to Cormac and speak to him to finish the quest.
Congratulations, quest complete!
After the quest, your boat should be docked at the island, but there is a chance it may still be in the cavern.
If your boat is still in the cavern, you can relog to spawn on it.

Tip: You may now utilise teleportation options to the island, as well as construct the bank chest in the building with Muriel. This requires a sunstone crystal that was dropped by the Mad Angel; it may be collected from Cormac if lost. The additional materials required are 2 lead bars, 8 mahogany planks, 32 mithril nails, a saw, and a hammer.

Talk to Dimintheis in a house south-east of the east bank (along city wall) in Varrock and north of the fancy dress shop. (Hi, I am a bold adventurer. → So where is this crest? → Ok, I will help you.)
Head to Catherby and talk to Caleb in the building north-east of the bank. (Are you Caleb Fitzharmon? → So can I have your bit? → Ok, I will get those.)
Speak to him again and give him all the fish. Note: Ask of the whereabouts of the other crest parts, or you will not be able to progress!(Uh... what happened to the rest of it?)
Speak to the Gem Trader in Al Kharid. (I'm in search of a man named Avan Fitzharmon.)
Go north of the Gem Trader to the scorpion mining pit, and speak to the 'Man' with the yellow cape there (Avan). (I'm looking for a man named Avan Fitzharmon.)
Head into the Dwarven Mine underneath Ice Mountain and run to the far most western end and speak to Boot. (Hello. I'm in search of very high quality gold.)

Teleport to Ardougne, head east and climb down the old ruin entrance to the Witchaven Dungeon near Witchaven and Ardougne ship port. (Labelled on the world map by the icon. You may need to defend yourself against some hellhounds, so come prepared).
Enter the dungeon. Do not enter the wall to the east. There is a north room, a south room, and a locked eastern room that contains hellhounds and the perfect gold ore.
To unlock the east gate:
Go to the north and lift the [[lever (Family Crest)
Then to the south room through the eastern door and lift that lever (up). Exit through the western door.
Back north and pull the outer lever (down), enter and lift the inner lever (up)
Exit the room and lift the lever (up)
Enter the south room by the western door and lower the lever (down). Exit through the eastern door.

Go into the hellhound room and mine 2 'perfect' gold ores. Their aggro range is short so try to zigzag through them. Anticipating hits will manageably yield the ores with a rune pickaxe. Alternatively, low level players can stand in a safespot for 10 minutes so the hellhounds stop being aggressive.
Go to a furnace (northern Lumbridge - use the home teleport) and smelt the ores into bars, then use the bars on the furnace again and make one [['perfect' necklace
Go back to the 'Man' (Avan) and give him the jewellery to receive the second crest piece.

Teleport to Varrock (lumberyard teleport), and head north-east to the Jolly Boar Inn near the lumberyard. Go upstairs and speak to Johnathon. Speak to him, and use your anti-poison on him to learn the location of the final crest piece.
Prepare for the fight:
Bring runes for each of the four blast spells: Wind Blast, Water Blast, Earth Blast, and Fire Blast as you need to deal damage with each spell.
Be aware that Chronozon's fight takes place in part of the Wilderness and other players may attack you there.
Maging is recommended. You will have to kill a poison spider to use the safespots, so anti-poison is recommended.
Diary tasks: Since Chronozon is at the [[Obelisk of Earth
Go to Edgeville or the small hut west of Varrock if you have a brass key to enter the Edgeville Dungeon.
Head to the gate dividing the Wilderness from the rest of the dungeon.
Travel slightly north, then make a left past the thugs and Chaos druids, through a second gate.
Travel west, then south past the poison spiders and Black demons, where you will find Chronozon.
Safespot him between the southern rocks. You may have to kill a poison spider first.
You must successfully cast each blast spell on Chronozon (No splashes or zeroes. Twinflame Staff will prohibit you from changing spells).
Once he has been weakened by each blast spell, kill him with any spell, melee, or ranged.
Pick up the last crest piece and teleport out.
Assemble the Family crest and head back to Dimintheis in Varrock to conclude.
Congratulations, quest complete!

To begin, talk with Dimintheis, who lives in south-eastern Varrock, within the fenced off area, in the house just above the clothes shop. Tell him you are a bold adventurer and he will propose an adventure for you; he needs his family crest returned. Ask him where the crest is, and he will explain his three sons took it with them when they rode out to battle many years ago. He hadn't heard from them since, until he recently learned that his son Caleb was working as a chef beyond the White Wolf Mountain, in Catherby.
Shrimps, bass, salmon, tuna and a swordfish (all cooked).

Head to Catherby, where Caleb can be found either inside the building with the sink to the south of the Farming shop, or wandering outside of it. Talk to him and ask if he is Caleb Fitzharmon, and he will tell you he has a 'bit' of the crest. Ask him what happened to the rest of it, and he will explain that he and his brothers broke the crest into three parts after a disagreement about who would become heir to their fathers' lands, and each of them ended up with a piece. Ask if you can have his bit of the crest, and he will agree to give you his piece provided you bring him ingredients for his fish salad. Agree to bring him the ingredients.
Note: You must ask him what happened to the rest of the crest, or you will be unable to collect the other parts.
Bring him the shrimp, salmon, tuna, bass, and swordfish (all cooked) and he will give you his piece of the crest.
necklace mould, ring mould, any pickaxe, 2 [[Ruby
Caleb mentioned that the last he heard from his brother Avan, he was searching for treasure in the desert, and that you might want to ask the traders there about him.

Head to the gem trader in the north of Al Kharid, found next to the gnome glider just south of the gate to Lumbridge. Ask him about Avan Fitzharmon, and he will remember that the man was searching for 'perfect gold'. The gem trader told him to search the sand dunes where gold rocks can be found. Head to the northern Al Kharid Mine, and a man can be found wandering around just at the entrance to the pit with a yellow cape on. This is, indeed, Avan, as he'll tell you when you ask him. He's not giving up his piece of the crest though unless you can help him win the affection of a certain lady by getting him a ring and necklace made out of perfect gold. Unfortunately, the stuff there in the desert isn't nearly good enough. He'll tell you a dwarf named Boot might know something about where to find the gold.
Note: The player must speak to Boot before being able to give the jewellery to Avan, even though it is possible to mine and smith perfect jewellery without speaking to him.

Head to the Dwarven Mines, located just west of the Edgeville Monastery. Climb down the trapdoor behind the eastern building to enter the mines. Boot can be found south-west from this northern entrance, wandering by the two rock columns - see the map to the right. Tell him you are in search of very high quality gold, and he will direct you to east of Ardougne, underground somewhere. The location you need to visit is the Witchaven Dungeon in Witchaven.

Note: You will need to pass by level 28 hobgoblins, level 53 ogres, and level 122 hellhounds in this dungeon, though you do not need to kill any of them. The hobgoblins will attack you immediately after entering the dungeon if below 57 Combat Level, and you will need to solve a puzzle while being attacked by ogres (if below 107 combat level). Protect from Melee will negate all damage, as the monsters only use melee.

Enter the dungeon and head north east along the path. To the north and south are two rooms with levers in and outside of them. You'll have to complete a lever puzzle here to unlock the eastern area which contains the gold rocks and hellhounds:
Go to the northern room and pull the outside lever up.
Head into the southern room using the eastern door, pull the lever up, then exit via the western door.
Go to the northern room and pull the outside lever down, then enter and pull the inner lever up.
Leave the room and pull the outside lever up again.
Go back to the southern room through the western door and pull the lever down, then exit via the eastern door.
The hellhound room should now be unlocked.
Note: Once unlocked, you do not need to do the puzzle again to re-enter.

Enter the hellhound room to the east and mine at least two 'perfect' gold ore from the gold rocks (40 Mining). The hellhounds have a short aggression range - try and zigzag past them to find an open rock to mine. If you draw aggression before you are done mining, there is a safespot you can use to hide in behind the rock column directly south of the entrance - you can then world hop to lose aggression and try again. Low levelled players may also consider waiting 10 minutes in this safespot, after which the hellhounds will not attack you while mining the southern rocks. The rocks will take some time to respawn, so once you have mined one rock, use another or world hop to reset the rock.

Once you have your two 'perfect' gold ore, head to any furnace with the ore, your rubies, your ring mould, and your necklace mould. You may consider using the one in Al Kharid, as you will be returning to Avan in the Al Kharid mine afterwards. Smelt the ore into 'perfect' gold bars (40 Smithing), then smelt a bar each into a ruby necklace and ruby ring respectively (40 Crafting, 40 Smithing), which will make the 'perfect' ring and 'perfect' necklace (DO NOT SELECT the GOLD necklace and ring!).
Return to Avan in the Al Kharid Mine, and he will take your jewellery and give you the second piece of the crest in return. He will then tell you how to find the final brother Johnathon.

The last brother is holed up on the of the Jolly Boar Inn north-east of Varrock near the edge of the Wilderness. Bring your antipoison potion, and head up to the where he is huddled in the north western room. Talk to him and he will be delirious - he has been bitten by a poisonous spider. Once he has finished speaking, use the antipoison on him (he'll take the entire potion, but you may bring a lower dosed potion) and he'll be very grateful to be cured.

Johnathon will tell you that he lost the crest while attempting to kill a powerful demon named Chronozon. If you want it back, you'll have to kill the demon yourself. Johnathon explains that to defeat the demon, you will need to first hit him once with each of the four elemental spells of death.
Chronozon can be found in the Edgeville Dungeon, by the poison spiders near the Earth obelisk.
Warning: You will be heading into the Wilderness, where other players may kill you. Only take items you are willing to lose to player killers, and consider using a low population world.

To defeat Chronozon, you will need to cast Wind Blast, Water Blast, Earth Blast, and Fire Blast and successfully hit him once with each (in any order). Chronozon weakens.... will appear in the chat after each individual hit from a blast spell. You do not need to kill him using Magic after he has been weakened, though he has no Magic defence and is weak to Water spells.

Along with enough runes to cast each blast spell several times, bring food, combat equipment and a poison cure for the poison spiders near Chronozon. Head to Edgeville and enter the dungeon through the trapdoor in the south eastern corner of the building south of the bank. Head north, then east through the gate past the skeletons, then north through the gate with thugs on the other side. Continue north past the thugs, west past the red spiders and black demons, then south to the Obelisk of Earth.

There is a safespot one square in front of the eastern standing torch for Magic and Ranged. If you draw aggression of the poison spiders, stand behind the stalagmite to avoid it, then hop worlds. Weaken him with each blast spell, then kill him with any combat style.
Note: If you take too long to kill him, his weakness will wear off and you'll have to weaken him again.
The Twinflame staff's double cast feature does not kill him as expected.
Chronozon will drop the final crest piece on death, pick it up.

Now that you have all three crest pieces, put them together to make the Family Crest and then make your way back to Varrock. Give the crest to Dimintheis who will be very, very pleased to have it back.
Congratulations, quest complete!
Tip: You may choose to talk to Dimintheis again to start the Family Pest miniquest before imbuing one of the gauntlets, as you will additionally have the chat option to progress the miniquest.
Talk to Ali Morrisane next to the Silk Stall in Al Kharid. (If you are, then why are you still selling goods from a stall? → I'd like to help you but..... → Yes. → Okay.)
Buy a kharidian headpiece and a fake beard and combine them.
Head to Pollnivneach.
Use the 3 beers on Drunken Ali at the bar. (Make sure to use one beer on him, then talk to him in full, then use the second beer, talk in full, then finally the third beer, and talk in full.)
Note: Don't skip dialogue after giving a beer. You can buy them from Ali the Barman.
Talk to the [[Bandit (Pollnivneach)
Go west of the bar and question the Menaphite Thugs.
Head to the camel store just north-west of the bar.

Talk to Ali the Camel Man to buy the camels for 500 coins. You will need two free spaces in your inventory. (Are those camels around the side for sale? → What price do you want for both of them? → Would 500 gold coins for the pair of them do?)
Talk to a Menaphite and a bandit to give them each a [[Receipt (The Feud)
Go to Ali the Operator and ask to join his gang (big purple tent, south-west)(Yes, of course, those bandits should be taught a lesson. → No thanks.)
Attempt to pickpocket a villager once then return to Ali the Operator. (Yeah, I could do with a bit of advice. → No thanks.)
Talk to the street urchin near the centre town well.
Pay him ten coins
Pickpocket the villager with an arrow over their head.
Talk to Ali the Operator (Yeah, I could do with a bit of advice.)
Equip the oak blackjack and then lure a villager into a secluded area.
Knock out the villager with the blackjack equipped
Pickpocket the villager
Talk to Ali the Operator.
Put on the desert disguise and gloves.
Hide behind the large cactus near the mayor's house (the large house to the East by the fountain).
Use the keys on the door.
Go up the stairs in the north-eastern corner.
Search the landscape picture near the bed.
Hit the button on the dial to reset it.
Click on 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, in that order, clockwise.
Give the jewels to Ali the Operator.
Talk to Ali the Operator.
Talk to a Menaphite Thug.
Talk to Ali the Operator. (No thanks.)
Talk to Ali the barman. (I'm looking for Traitorous Ali. → No thanks I'm ok.)
Buy special sauce from the kebab seller. He can be found north-west of the well in the middle of the town. (Would you sell me that bottle of special kebab sauce? → No thanks, I'm good.)
Use it on a trough behind the camel shop.
Use a bucket on the dung if it is brown. Obtain three more buckets of dung if you plan to complete My Arm's Big Adventure.

Use a coin on the snake charmer's money pot, sitting south of the bar (Wow, a snake charmer. Can I have a go? Can I have a go? Please?) with 2 free inventory spaces to get a snake charm and a snake basket.
Use the snake charm on a desert snake north of the Menaphite tent until it goes into the snake basket.
