Go to Glough's house, and use the key to open the chest and take the invasion plans.
Take the invasion plans to the king. He will give you four letters made of sticks (you'll need 4 empty inventory spaces).
Climb the watchtower in Glough's house (tree in the east part of his house). Use the sticks with the four pillars to spell out TUZO. If you are under 25 Agility, eat your summer pie now.
Bank if needed and prepare for the battle, then go down the trapdoor.
After you enter and talk to Glough, a level 172 [[Black demon (The Grand Tree)

Immediately after the cutscene ends, run to the tile directly north of the ladder. The black demon will become stuck behind the daconia rocks in front of you as he approaches. Attack with ranged, magic, or a halberd.

Warning: The demon will despawn after a while if it is not killed within 10 minutes exactly. If this happens, you'll have to exit through the ladder in the centre of the cave and go through Glough's trapdoor again.
Kill the demon. Walk along the passage until you find [[King Narnode Shareen
Talk to the king, and he will ask you to locate the last daconia rock. Fully complete the dialogue; otherwise, you cannot continue.
Search the [[Root (The Grand Tree)
Talk to the king one last time.
Congratulations, quest complete!

Ensure you have two free inventory slots, then speak to King Narnode Shareen on the of the Grand Tree. He will take you underground to show you the roots of the tree, which appear to be dying. He will give you a translation book and a bark sample and ask you to take the sample to Hazelmere, the last surviving gnome mage involved in creating the tree.
Hazelmere is found on a small island east of Yanille, upstairs in his house. There are jungle spiders (level 44) on the way, although they are not poisonous.
Talk to Hazelmere, who will take your bark sample, and after examining it, give you a message written in his language.
Return to King Narnode in the Grand Tree, who will ask what the translation is. The correct translation can be deciphered using the translation book and reads:
A man came to me with the King's seal. I gave the man [[Daconia stone

Give him the correct translation from the options offered, selecting none of the above for the first two choices. (I think so. → None of the above. → None of the above. → A man came to me with the King's seal. → I gave the man Daconia rocks. → And Daconia rocks will kill the tree!)

The king will exclaim that someone must have forged his seal to obtain the Daconia rocks, which were made as a "fail-safe" and are the only thing that can kill the tree. He will direct you to talk to Glough, his head tree guardian.
1,000 coins (if you haven't helped Femi)

Glough is located in a treehouse south of the Grand Tree, east of the ramp by the hot air balloon. After remarking that humans can't be trusted, he will tell you that he will take care of the problem.
Return to King Narnode Shareen, who informs you that Glough has caught and imprisoned a human found with the Daconia rocks.

Head to the top floor to speak with Charlie the prisoner. He tells you that Glough paid him to retrieve the rocks from Hazelmere. He doesn't know what Glough is up to, but suggests you search Glough's house for evidence.

Go to Glough's house and search the cupboard to find his journal, which describes how he plans to convince the tree gnomes that humans are naturally evil and must be destroyed. Confront Glough, who calls a guard over to lock you in the cell next to Charlie's. Talk to Charlie, who mentions he delivered a large amount of gold to the shipyard on Karamja. He suggests you give the foreman there a visit to covertly see if he knows what Glough is up to, and gives you the password to access it, which is Ka-Lu-Min.

The king will appear and apologise for Glough imprisoning you. He will tell you that guards are watching the entrances, and tells you to quickly escape on the Gnome glider on the top floor of the Grand Tree, next to the cells. Talk to the pilot. He will ask you where you want to go and you will ask him to fly you to Karamja.
left

The glider will crash land just west of the Shipyard. Run east, avoiding the aggressive level 53 jogres, and attempt to open the gate to the Shipyard. A shipyard worker will stop you; tell him Glough sent you, then give him the password Ka-Lu-Min.
Once inside, find the level 23 foreman on the southern docks. You may either kill him or talk to him to receive a lumber order.
If you choose to talk to him, tell him Glough sent you, then answer some personal questions about Glough. He will ask how his wife is, select "Sadly his wife is no longer with us".
He will then ask what his favourite dish is, select "Worm holes".
Finally, he will ask for his new girlfriend's name, which is "Anita". (Sadly his wife is no longer with us! → He loves worm holes. → Anita.)

You need to return to the Grand Tree to show the king the lumber order which is evidence of Glough's invasion plans, but Glough has ordered the guards not to let you in. You can now teleport out of the shipyard and head to the Gnome Stronghold, or leave via the charter ship if you brought coins. If you have completed the Tree Gnome Village quest, you can sneak in by using a spirit tree, such as the one at the Grand Exchange or the Battlefield.

Alternatively, talk to Femi by the gate to the stronghold. Tell her you need to get inside, and she will sneak you in. She will help you for free if you never entered the stronghold through the gate before, or if you chose to help her move boxes the first time you entered. If you chose not to help her when you first entered, she will charge you 1,000 coins.
Lumber order
After you show the king the note from the foreman, he still will not believe your accusations, call you as paranoid as Glough, and ask you to leave for your own safety.

Speak to Charlie the prisoner again on the top floor of the Grand Tree, who says he heard Glough mention a chest key that he left at his girlfriend Anita's house. In the north-west corner of the stronghold, climb up the most north-western ladder by the tortoise pens to speak to Anita and she will give you Glough's key and ask you to return it to him.
Go to Glough's house, and use the key to open the chest. Inside, you will find his invasion plans detailing his plan to seize control of Gielinor. Click continue to receive the plans.

Ensure you have four free inventory spaces, then take the invasion plans to the king. He will still not believe you, stating that anyone could have made the plans. He will give you four bundles of twigs, which was all his guards could find when searching Glough's house.

Return to Glough's house, and climb up the watchtower. This tree is located on the east side of the by the chest and requires 25 Agility to climb. Up in the watchtower, you will find a stone stand and four pillars. Use the twigs with the four pillars to spell out TUZO, starting from the far left. Using the Translation book, this translates to "open." After you have placed the twigs on the four pillars, you will hear gears turning, activating the trap door on this platform, but do not go in yet unless you are prepared for the fight.
left

Climb down the trapdoor into the cave below, and Glough will appear, threatening you with his plans to wipe out humans. Complete the conversation without interacting with anything else, or you will have to re-enter and repeat it. A level 172 black demon will appear down the tunnel and immediately attack you.

It can be fought with any combat style, but can be safespotted with Ranged, Magic or a halberd. To safespot, immediately move one tile to the north and then east (adjacent to the ladder, see the picture).
Magic is recommended, as the demon has a negative magic defence bonus. Use water spells if available to you as it has a 40% weakness to water spells.

Note: If the demon is not killed within 10 minutes, it will disappear and the battle needs to be restarted. To do so, walk through the tunnel and leave through the ladder next to King Narnode Shareen, and re-enter Glough's trapdoor.

Note for 10HP pures: With Bind, it is possible to kill the demon with a cannon with at least 120 cannonballs. When the scene begins, use Bind on the demon immediately and set up the cannon just 2-3 spaces west of the ladder you used to enter. If you die during setup the cannon will remain. You will know the cannon is in the right area if you can reload it from the ladder safespot. If the cannon aggros a rat during the fight without killing it, the cannon may stop firing, and you will need to take aggro from the demon by moving forward and back, or lure the rat away.

After defeating the demon, Glough will flee into the tunnel behind him. Walk along the passage until you find King Shareen standing by a ladder. Talk to him and tell him that Glough sent a demon to attack you. Not believing you, he will finally send a guard to scout for Glough, finding him hiding amongst the stones. The king apologises, and asks you to locate the last Daconia rock.

Ensure you have one free inventory space, then search the roots all around the area until you find the Daconia rock. It may be in any of the roots, so keep going until you have found the rock. Click continue once you find it or it won't appear in your inventory. If you somehow lose the rock, it'll spawn in the root where you first found it.
Talk to King Shareen again for your reward for saving the Grand Tree.
Congratulations, quest complete!
Note: Don't bring any pets!

Go south a bit to the monastery and use the keg and fuse on the door. Light the fuse.
Enter and kill 4 Sorebones for a Cranial clamp, Brain tongs, 3 Bell jars, and 30 Skull staples.
Climb-down the ladder in the mill and talk to Dr Fenkenstrain.
Climb up and talk to Brother Tranquility, prepare for the fight.
Return to the Harmony island monastery and Confront Mi-Gor to start the fight against Barrelchest.
You must wear your equipment to breathe underwater.
Each attack will disable your prayer and remove a few prayer points.
When adjacent he will only attack with melee.
Re-enabling prayer after each attack will prevent you from taking any damage.
Alternatively you can leave the monastery and re-enter; the boss will get stuck and can be safespotted from the entrance.
Talk to Brother Tranquility.
Congratulations, quest complete!
Note: Leave your follower in the bank, otherwise you will not be able to go diving.

To start the quest, you must sail to Mos Le'Harmless and speak to Brother Tranquility. To get there, use a Mos le'harmless teleport, a Trouble Brewing mini-game teleport, or talk to Bill Teach on his boat in Port Phasmatys at the east end of the dock near the Green Ghost Inn and agree to sail to Mos Le'Harmless.

Near the dock, you will notice a rather sickly-looking monk named Brother Tranquility. Talk to him to begin the quest — select the option regarding undead pirates. He will explain how some of his fellow monks are in trouble and ask for help. Accept the offer to be teleported to Harmony Island.
When doing the Hard Morytania Diary, you can plant your watermelon seeds now, so you can harvest them at the end of the quest.

Make sure you have the supplies listed earlier and head outside the windmill. Zombie pirates (level 57) are aggressive and will attack. A short way to the north will be a Saradomin statue that can be pulled. Pull the statue. Go down the hole and into a tunnel. It is full of water, so equip the underwater breathing gear to submerge beneath the water. Note that you cannot enter the water if you are carrying a follower such as a pet cat. Run past the zombie pirates and repair the stairs at the far end of the tunnel (you can be attacked while repairing the stairs and it takes a while). Go up them, climb up the ladder in the next room; then, look through the peephole to spy on the enemy.
Holy symbol.

Report back to Brother Tranquility. He will suggest getting a book that can be used to pray away poison. Travel to the Monastery near Edgeville to find the prayer book in a bookshelf towards the south-west corner of the building on the . Read the book, which provides instructions on how to use it. Equip a holy symbol and return to Harmony Island by talking to Brother Tranquility. The zombies have begun to gas the windmill, so right-click the book and select "recite-prayer." After this, make sure to talk to Brother Tranquility.
tablet equivalents]], [[Kharyrll teleport (tablet)

Now that the monks are no longer in danger of being poisoned, they would like to get their brains back in their bodies where they belong. Travel to Dr Fenkenstrain in his castle, climb up either stairs, and then climb up the ladder in the jail cell in the middle of the room. After a bit of negotiation, he agrees that a new home free of the threat of being eaten sounds better than where he is. However, he does not want to risk being eaten while travelling. He is also allergic to teleportation, so another way needs to be found.

Go to Canifis and talk to Rufus, the owner of the meat store north of the bank, about another meat shipment. Make sure to be wearing the Ring of Charos while talking to him. Rufus will give you some crate parts and a wolf whistle. You need to build ten decoy cats to fill the crate since Rufus assumes the crate will be transporting cats.

Tip: Since you are right next to a bank, deposit the whistle and crate parts and take out Mos Le'Harmless teleport (treasure trail), 10 wooden planks, 10 pieces of fur, and a hammer — home teleport runes or tab and an ectophial are advised for easy travelling. If you do not have a Clockmaker's bench yet, you will also need to bring 4 oak planks and a saw. Also, if you still need fur, you can kill Canifis villagers—they'll transform into level 88 werewolves if you don't use Wolfbane, so be careful. You can also obtain fur by thieving from stalls in Ardougne (or trading with the fur trader there) or by purchasing fur in Varrock Square for 20 coins apiece. Ultimate Ironmen may find a table in the south-west tower of Fenkenstrain's castle on the first floor helpful.

Travel to a player-owned house that has a Clockmaker's bench. Craft the materials into 10 wooden cats. Grab your Ring of Charos, the 10 wooden cats, 4 planks (normal), a hammer, ~50 nails, the crate parts, and the wolf whistle before travelling back to Fenkenstrain's castle.

Return to Dr Fenkenstrain and build the crate on the crate hotspot. Then select the "add-bottom" option on the crate to build the false bottom of the crate. If you run out of nails whilst building the surround or the bottom, you will have to start over and bring more nails to ensure the structure is built. Fill it with the fake cats and then use the wolf whistle Rufus gave you to call him. Fenkenstrain will automatically get in the crate.
Tip: You can't blow the Wolf whistle if you are still wearing the Fishbowl helmet.
Once past inspection, Rufus will give you a shipping order. Use this on the crate, and it will be teleported to the island.

Now that the doctor is on the island, travel back to Mos Le'Harmless. Use the island bank to grab a hammer, equipment to breath underwater, armour, and a weapon before teleporting to Harmony Island. Dr Fenkenstrain is in the basement of the windmill and needs some equipment to perform the surgery. He will give you a list of items to collect:
Brain tongs
Cranial clamp
3 bell jars
30 skull staples
A hammer
Luckily, the bad guys already have what you need since they performed the surgery in the first place. The only problem is how to get inside the building.

Put on the equipment to breathe underwater to avoid passing out from the gas, and head north from the windmill to the ship beached nearby. Search the locker on the to get a fuse; then, climb up a level and get a tinderbox and a keg of powder. With these in hand, go back to the front door of the monastery. Use the keg in the front door, add a fuse, and then, light it. The door is now open.

Once inside, kill the 4 Sorebones to obtain all the needed equipment, which can be safespotted behind benches. You must pick up the dropped items after each kill, or else you will just get duplicates. Walk back to the windmill, head downstairs, and give all this to Dr Fenkenstrain to begin the gruesome surgery. A cutscene of a cute cat playing with a ball will ensue due to the surgery being too gruesome. Make sure to speak to Brother Tranquility after the operation.
Note, the Sorebones are considered Undead and thus a Salve amulet will work against them.

Return to the bank on Mos Le'Harmless and grab all the armour, food, and potions you will need for the fight. Note: You still need to wear your underwater equipment. The Barrelchest is NOT considered Undead meaning the Salve amulet will not provide a benefit against him.
Go back to Harmony.

When you enter the monastery, only Mi-Gor will be there, giving you the option to confront him. When you do, he will summon his monstrosity, a giant mess of machinery named Barrelchest, to attack you.
Prayer (and also Defence) drains faster than usual during the fight, and Barrelchest will turn your Prayers off.

If meleeing, just keep turning prayer back on (note: repeatedly turning it on can be a huge time waste and result in death if he gets lucky with the timing of his hits, plan to do this without prayer to avoid that). Bringing several prayer potions and at least ten good food is highly recommended. Barrelchest is a fairly blunt instrument; he will not use anything but Melee attacks, which are fairly slow and inaccurate; however, when he does hit, he tends to frequently hit over 20.

If ranging or maging, it is possible to safespot him: either catch him on the corner of the first pew by taking a few steps back when you first start the battle, or simply exit and then re-enter the monastery after the fight begins and he will immediately be caught if you stay where you are at the entrance. DO NOT hide behind a pew when attempting to do this or he will strike the ground with his anchor, dealing up to 25 typeless Ranged damage.
Once you have killed Barrelchest, pick up his anchor and walk back to the windmill to inform Brother Tranquility of your victory.
He will thank you and give you a lamp granting 5,000 experience in the skill of your choice.
Congratulations, quest complete!
Note: If you died during the boss fight, you will need another set of underwater equipment to recover your items. Otherwise, you'll need to visit Death in his office.

Talk to Sylas.
Congratulations, quest complete!
Talk to Bert in Yanille, in the house next to the POH Portal to get a Sandy hand. (Eww a hand, in the sand! Why haven't you told the authorities? → Yes.)
Go to the Dragon Inn pub south of Bert's house. Buy a beer from the bartender (if you don't have one) and give the beer to the Guard Captain.

Ring the bell at the Wizards' Guild (outside near eastern doors), or enter the guild with 66 Magic, then talk to Zavistic Rarve, who will take the Hand. If started Zogre Flesh Eaters: (I have a rather sandy problem that I'd like to palm off on you.)

Talk to Betty in Port Sarim Magic shop for a bottled water. (Talk to Betty about the Hand in the Sand.)
First add redberries, then white berries to the bottled water in order to get a pink dye.
Redberries can be bought at the food store in southern Port Sarim.
Dye the lantern lens to get a rose-tinted lens.
Talk to Betty again so she puts the vial on the counter. (Talk to Betty about the Hand in the Sand.)
Go stand in the doorway and "use" the lens on the counter to get a truth serum.
Talk to Betty one last time with sand in your inventory. (Talk to Betty about the Hand in the Sand.)
Travel to Brimhaven and talk to Sandy.

Select an option until you distract him, and use the truth serum on Sandy's Coffee Mug. (There's a herd of huge mutant herring about to drop from the sky! → But the pygmy shrews have eaten all the sand! → A small parrot with a pink banana is sitting outside your window!)

Activate the magical orb and talk to Sandy again. Be sure to click every option. (Why is Bert's rota different from the original? → Why doesn't Bert remember the change in his hours? → What happened to the wizard?)

Talk to Zavistic Rarve again to get a cut scene.

Return to Yanille, ring the bell and talk to Zavistic Rarve.
Beer

Start the quest by talking to Bert in Yanille in the building just east of the POH portal. He works in the sandpit but has found a severed hand and is afraid to tell the authorities for fear of losing his job. Agree to lend him a hand and you will receive a sandy hand. He'll tell you to go talk to the captain of the guards. He hangs around the inn in Yanille, usually drunk.

Take the hand to the captain of the guards in the Ye Olde Dragon Inn; he'll demand a beer. Give him a pint; a cheap beer can be bought from the bartender for two coins. He will ramble on, and then, he'll take a look at the hand and accidentally drop it in his beer, turning it into a beer soaked hand. He suggests it was probably the wizards who did it and suggest you ring the bell of their guild and talk to 'the first pointy hatted ninny you shee.'

Go to the Wizards' Guild, east of the bar; enter if you meet the requirements (66 Magic), or ring the bell to make Zavistic Rarve come out. Talk to him to wave the hand in front of his face and enquire whether the guild still has all of its wizards. You explain the situation and hand him the hand. He will tell you that this is the hand of one of his wizard students, Clarence. He'll ask you to see if Bert's working schedule has changed recently, for he has been working rather long hours recently.

Return to Bert's home and talk to him again. He'll tell you that he works for Sandy's Sand Corp, which is based in Brimhaven, by hauling sand from there to the pit in Yanille. He'll give you a copy of his schedule and tell you that it hasn't changed recently, or so he thinks. Now, you need to head to Sandy in Brimhaven to compare Bert's rota with the original. You can go to Ardougne and pay 30 coins to get to Brimhaven. Sandy is located in the office just north-west of the Dead Man's Chest bar.

In Brimhaven, you'll see Sandy in his office. You can talk to him first if you want, but this isn't necessary. Search his desk in the house to get Bert's old schedule. Read it and compare it to the other schedule to see that Bert has indeed been working longer hours. While you're here, pickpocket Sandy to find some sand in his pocket — this may take multiple attempts. Keep it; it will become important later on in the quest.

Now, you need to visit Bert once more. Talk to Bert in Yanille to inform him of his changed hours. He will not remember it and blame it on the wizards and the magic leaking from their nearby guild. You give him the rotas in exchange for a magic scroll that appeared in his house recently. He instructs you to see whether 'those infernal wizards' are up to anything.

Take the scroll to Zavistic Rarve at the Wizards' Guild to learn that it's a mind-altering scroll, explaining why Bert doesn't remember his hours' changing. You suspect Sandy is behind it and Zavistic asks you to first get Betty in Port Sarim to make you a truth serum and then record Sandy using the magical orb he gives you. If you ask him to help you more, he will teleport you to Betty's shop just once in exchange for an empty vial.

Betty can be found in a small shop marked by the icon on the minimap. Talk to Betty about the quest and she will ask for another empty vial. In return, she gives you some bottled water. You need to add redberries to make redberry juice, then add white berries to make pink dye. Once you've made some, use it on a lantern lens to create a rose-tinted lens.

Talk to Betty again. She tells you to stand in the doorway while the door is open and shine your lens at the counter to focus the light on an empty vial whilst she pours the truth serum into it. Do so by clicking on the lens in your inventory, then using it on the counter. This will heat up and shatter the lens. Speak to Betty again; you now need a personal item from Sandy for the potion to work.

Return to Sandy's office and pickpocket him to get some loose sand if you had not already. Return to Betty for her to finish the serum with the handful of sand. She warns you that you should dilute the serum in tea or coffee or else 'bits' might drop off the drinker.
Make sure to buy five earth runes from Betty before you leave if you don't have them already.
Truth serum, magical orb

Back in Brimhaven, return to Sandy. He has a mug of steaming coffee next to him, but will require distraction for you to be able to add the truth serum. Get him distracted with tall tales of herds of giant mutant herrings and pygmy shrews. Try all the options, as there is no guaranteed one that will work. Once he looks out the window, use the serum on his coffee. He will drink it. Next, activate your magical orb and talk to him.

He'll confess that he bribed a wizard to put a mind-altering spell on Bert. He then changed Bert's schedule so that he'd work longer for the same salary. Afterwards, Sandy killed the wizard so that he wouldn't have to pay him; then, he buried parts of him in all of the sandboxes around Gielinor. This fills the magical orb; return to Zavistic in Yanille to show him the evidence.
5 earth runes, a bucket of sand.

Hand Zavistic Rarve the magical orb in your inventory - it is proof of Sandy's confession. He asks for five earth runes and a bucket of sand, refusing to tell you why. Bring these to him. A bucket can be filled at Bert's sandpit if necessary. He will then cast a spell on Bert's sandpit to magically refill itself to compensate Bert for his troubles. He will no longer have to work! Zavistic says he has sent wizards around the various sandpits of RuneScape to find the remains of Clarence and asks you to check on the Entranan one.

Go to Entrana (there is a bank deposit box at Port Sarim to deposit all armour and weapons before going to the holy island). Talk to Mazion by the sandpit to get the dead wizard's head. Give this to Zavistic Rarve. He'll confirm that it belongs to Clarence and that the wizard will be buried the same day. He has also sent word for Sandy to be arrested and gives you a reward for your help.
Congratulations, quest complete!
Tip: Speak to Bert right after completing the quest to complete a medium Ardougne Diary task.

Run directly west through the cave and crawl-through the cart tunnel.

Climb up the ladder and start saving your run energy after you turn the water valve in the next step.

Head south and use the Zealot's key on the water valve.
Note: If you forgot a chisel be sure to grab the one near the lift before you open the valve; you won't have enough time to pick it up while running there.
Quickly run to the lift and take it down.
Go south then East and down the stairs.
Go through the door.
Pick up the innocent-looking key to start the boss fight.

Kill Treus Dayth. It is recommended to pray Protect from Missiles throughout the fight. A good way to fight this boss is to run near him after attacking; the goal is to force him into the north-eastern corner. Once this occurs, run west to the end of the detached northern shaft and attack him from a distance. This prevents him from teleporting around the mine while also negating crane damage, which should make the fight easier.
Note: If you teleport away, you will have to get another Glowing fungus.
Note: If you die, you cannot get the Glowing fungus back from your grave in the flooded area. This is not a safe fight.
Note: If you are following the [[Optimal quest guide
Pick up the key
Go back up the eastern stairs.
Go west and down those stairs. You will need the Glowing fungus to act as a light source.
Open the door and cut the crystal outcrop to the south-east with your chisel.
Congratulations, quest complete!
Players can use a ball of wool on a salve shard to make a salve amulet.
The crystal-mine key, obtained after killing Treus Dayth, can be added to the steel key ring.
Unless the player has a low defence or prayer level, it is often more efficient to tank the crane hits and rush the boss directly than it is to spend time navigating the area.

Mining mithril ore within the abandoned mine is a hard task in the Morytania Diary. You can receive a pickaxe by attempting to take one of the pickaxes lying on the ground near the bottom of the lift, which will come to life (level 50) before dropping an Iron Pickaxe. There is also a spawn of a bronze pickaxe at the top of the lift, just to the west.

To begin the quest, players need to head to the Abandoned Mine, which can be found in the south-westernmost part of Morytania, south of the swamps and west of Mort'ton and Burgh de Rott. To reach the abandoned mine players will either have to have started Nature Spirit or have access to fast travel to Mort'ton or Barrows.

There is a low fence shortcut from Burgh de Rott which requires 25 Agility and partial completion of In Aid of the Myreque, which will save time not running through the swamp to the north of the mine.

Warning: The boss fight is very difficult even for higher combat levels, as you will take a lot of damage regardless of armour. The only nearby bank is the Burgh de Rott bank unlocked through In Aid of the Myreque, and returning to the boss fight room will require you to redo some steps of the quest, so it is recommended to bring all of your combat gear and supplies for the boss at the start of the quest. Read ahead to the boss fight section for tips.
Note: If travelling through the swamp to reach the mine, don't forget your filled druid pouch.

In the area between the mine and the swamp, a Saradominist zealot is walking around. Speak to him and he will demand to know your allegiance. Select any response other than Zamorak, and ask him what he is doing. He will explain that he is on a quest to reclaim the Haunted Mines in the name of Saradomin, and that the legendary Salve amulet, since lost, was carved from the crystals that grow in the lower levels of the mine. The mines are haunted by the condemned soul of Treus Dayth, a Zamorakian mage whose soul was bound by Zamorak to the mines to prevent those crystals from ever being reached again. The zealot hopes to reach these crystals to recreate the Salve amulet.

Ask about other entrances into the mine, and the zealot will confirm that a second entrance may exist, and that he has come into possession of a key granting access to the lower levels of the mine. Pickpocket him to get his key (drops on the floor with full inventory). Follow the cart track to the south (avoiding the the feral vampyres) and climb over the mine cart blocking the way, then enter the cart tunnel.
Note: If you don't have 15 Agility, you cannot climb over the cart - instead, go to the west side of the mountain and enter the southern entrance.
You find yourself in a dark cave with many bats, big and small, and many pickaxes and corpses strewn about. There are some hazards to be aware of throughout the mine:
Some skeletons are dormant; the ones called corpses in yellow letters will spring to life and become skeletal miners when you approach
Some pickaxes may become possessed and attack you when you attempt to pick them up
Creepy hazes are spooky but generally harmless (although they can sometimes turn into aggressive ghosts when adjacent to them)
Mine carts moving of their own accord will damage you if you get in their way

Your task is to make your way to the depths of the caves and find the Salve crystal. Follow the cart track to the west and exit the cave on the western side (ignore the ladder). Once outside, enter the southern entrance (the same one used if you didn't climb over the cart).
Climb down the ladder at the end of the blocked path. Head east and climb down the next ladder.

Follow the path to the cart track running north to south. Wait until the moving cart has headed south, then follow it and wait in the western alcove to the south. When the cart passes north, run south to the ladder and climb down.

After climbing down the ladder (12), you will arrive next to a stagnant pool to the west with glowing fungus growing (X). Pick one; this is to be your light source in the lowest level of the cave (no other light source will work). There is a lift to the east, but you cannot descend in it now - it leads to a flooded area which would extinguish any other light source. You will need to find a way to transport the fungi to the lift without carrying it, as it will crumble to ashes if taken outside.
Warning: Do not take the fungi outside of the cave and also do not drop it, as both actions will cause it to crumble to ashes. Random events that teleport the player will also destroy the fungi.
Head north-west along the track until you reach a searchable mine cart. Place the fungus in the cart (T). Head north and then west to the Points settings (P) panel, which operates the cart system.

Note: In the alcove immediately south of the panel is an Iron pickaxe. If you didn't bring a pickaxe but you plan to do the hard Morytania Diary task during the quest, you can pick this one up without it becoming possessed. Beware of the skeletal miner corpse becoming reanimated however.

Open the panel, and it will show a map of all the cart tracks on this level as well as ten junctions that can each be in two positions. Pressing the start button sets the cart system in motion. The objective is to get the cart from the start position on the left to the ladder in the top right corner (north-west).

The map also shows two groups of levers controlling the junctions. The cart will follow the crimson (lighter red) route at any junction when approaching from the tail direction of the corresponding arrow. Pulling the respective lever exchanges the crimson and burgundy arrows at the junction. The initial configuration will be different for each player, but the solution remains the same (see the image below).

The levers A through E are south-east of the control panel (location (Q) on the map above), whereas F through J are north, around the corner (location (R)). Beware of skeletal miners lying in ambush at both stations. The levers F, G and H are inaccessible, meaning those junctions are fixed.

When approaching a junction from the arrow head's direction, its orientation (i.e., colour) does not matter as long as it is a straight path. In order to round a corner and not plunge into a wall or the water, the direction taken by the cart must be marked by a crimson arrow.
Haunted Mine - Levers A-E.png|Levers A-E.
Haunted Mine - Levers I-K.png|Levers F-K. (The blocked levers F, G & H are unmarked in this picture.)
Haunted Mine - Track map.png|The mine cart route solution.

Operate all the levers in accordance with the rules above and then check the control panel to make sure that the route on your map directs the mine cart to the ladder. Operate the mine cart by pressing the start button and the map will show the path of the mine cart.
Depending on the contents and route of the cart, four outcomes are possible. They are indicated both by the second half of the short cutscene, and a game message or player dialogue:
Oh dear, the mine cart seems to have sunk. - The cart sinks into the water. Any fungus in the cart will be destroyed.
How useful, it's come right back to where it started. - The cart returns to the start. Any fungus in the cart will still be in the cart.
Player: I wonder if that cart is anywhere useful now? - The cart successfully makes it to the other side. The fungus will now be on the other side.
(No message) - The cart successfully makes it to the other side. There was no fungus in the cart before sending it.

If the cart sinks, the glowing fungus is removed from the cart. In that case, pick another glowing fungus and put it in the cart (T). Operate the appropriate levers to fix the problem and hit the red button again.

When the mine cart reaches the correct end point, you will remark that it may have ended up somewhere useful. If your character doesn't make a comment about the location of the cart, put another mushroom in and send the cart off again.

You will now have to reach the ladder yourself to retrieve the fungus. First, retrace your steps to the very top of the mine. Go back up the ladder (12) near the glowing fungi pool. Walk north along the track, avoiding the cart. Take the first path to the east and climb up the ladder at the end of the path. Go west and up the ladder, then exit the cave to the west. You should end up next to the River Salve.

Enter the northern cave. Climb down the first ladder immediately to the east and head north-east through the cave. Climb down the northern ladder to the next level. Head to the north-west corner of the cave and climb down the ladder.
Search the nearby cart and take the glowing fungus that was put in earlier. If there is no fungus in the cart, you will need to repeat the previous process.

Note: If you die during the boss fight, you will need to get another glowing fungus and send it through the mine cart again, but you will not need to set the levers again as they will remain the same.
Zealot's key, combat equipment and plenty of high-healing food

Do not take the mine cart track leading south. Instead, climb back up with the fungus in your possession. Head all the way east past the ladder going up and then south past a moving cart. Climb down the ladder to end up in a side cave east of the flooded tracks. Head south down the corridor. Pick up the chisel from the spawn on top of a crate if you did not bring one.

In this area there is a water-powered lift going further down but it is not operational. To use it, head around the large pipe and use the zealot's key on the valve to activate the water flow from the nearby basin. Run quickly back to the lift and head down, before a mischievous ghost can shut off the valve. If the ghost beats you, simply turn the valve again and retry.
Note: If you die during the following boss fight, you will not need to use the valve again, and the key is no longer required for access.

The lift will drop you into a pool of water, but the cave will be properly lit with the glowing fungus. From the flooded chamber, walk south onto the track (beware of possessed pickaxes) and follow the east track. Climb down the stairs (14) and go west into a large chamber with loading cranes and mine carts. This room is where the boss fight will take place.
Do not take the innocent-looking key until you are completely ready to begin!
Note: If you want to return to the upper levels, simply return to the lift, click on it and you will automatically swim towards it.

Note: Read this part fully before entering the fight if you're not experienced with the fight! Especially if you're low combat! This boss fight is difficult and should not be taken lightly. High-healing food is recommended. The surrounding environment is more dangerous than the actual boss itself.

To start the fight, try to pick up the innocent-looking key. It will float away and return. Click the chatbox to continue the dialogue and the ghost of Treus Dayth (combat level 95), the erstwhile guardian of the Salve crystals, will appear and start to attack you.

During the fight Treus will use his ghostly powers to turn invisible, and move through obstacles about the room. He cannot be attacked while invisible, and you will need to chase him around the room until he reappears. His location is at any time indicated by a flashing yellow arrow on the minimap. As the fight progresses he will disappear at a faster rate.
There are four methods that Treus uses to damage you:

Mine Cart - When the player steps on a cart track, a mine cart will be sent tumbling after them. This can hit up to 9 typeless damage every game tick, which can equal to 36 damage every 2 seconds if the player is unlucky. This is the most dangerous attack. This attack can be easily avoided by running across the tracks instead as the cart will only move when the player is in its target range.

Crane - The possessed cranes will attack the player if the player moves to a square directly adjacent to it, dealing up to 10 typeless damage. This is the second most dangerous attack out of the three.

Pickaxes - If the player is not near any other obstacle, the player will be attacked by projectile pickaxes. These hit up to 15 damage each. The Protect from Missiles prayer only provides 33% protection from this attack, reducing it to a max of 10. Pickaxes are the second least dangerous attack.
Melee - If the player is standing next to Treus Dayth, he may rarely use a melee attack that deals up to 8 damage. This is the least used attack and also the least dangerous.

As Treus moves around the room, you will need to chase him across the tracks without staying on them, and while avoiding standing too close to the cranes. Treus will throw pickaxes at you, so you should pray Protect from Missiles while running around, using stamina potions to keep your run energy, and restoring your hitpoints with food while he is invisible. Note that you can also leave via the eastern door at any time and use that as a safe zone to regenerate your health, run energy and prayer if necessary - the boss will have the same amount of health when you re-enter. The boss will eventually reset back to a key if the fight lasts too long.

If Treus moves between the north-western and north-eastern side of the room, you may run back and forth along the northern-most cart track where you only have to dodge one cart. If he moves south, try to hug the cavern walls to avoid the cranes as you approach him.

Magic is the easiest choice against this boss due to its low Magic defence; it is also weak to Wind spells and Crumble Undead. If you have access to an Iban's staff (requiring 50 Attack, Magic, and completion of Underground Pass) it may be more effective, as it hits accurately (especially against this boss) and very high. Note however that most of your attacks will take place in close to melee range, as the obstacles in the room will block you from attacking the boss at range. You can kill the boss with any combat style if you have a stronger option due to your combat stats or gear. If using magic, consider bringing along an additional set of defensive armour to switch to while running after the boss to reduce the damage of his Ranged attack. When he reappears you can switch back to your offensive Magic gear.

As you have limited opportunities to hit him, using a high hitting special attack like the dragon dagger as a secondary can be useful. Its special attack hits twice in one go, but this boss will only receive one of those hits before he moves away to a new spot and before you even get to him the second attack from the dagger will automatically hit him. If using melee as your primary attack style, bring the highest-hitting melee weapon you can use, such as a 2h sword or halberd.

Interestingly, Treus Dayth's attack speed while not teleporting is dramatically lowered to a 30-tick cycle if he is successfully poisoned. He is, however, immune to poison damage. You may consider using a trident of the swamp to apply venom.
Note: It is not possible to freeze the ghost from moving using Magic or the Zamorak Godsword special attack.

Note: If you die, items will appear inside a grave for 15 minutes. You will need to get another glowing fungus to return. The boss will respawn once you take the key again. If you fail to retrieve your grave in time your items will be at Death's Office.

After defeating Treus Dayth, the machinery will stop attacking you. Pick up the innocent-looking key, which no longer resists and is, in fact, the crystal-mine key. Now, head back east through the door and climb up the stairs back to Level 5. Walk all the way west until you reach another staircase (15) and head down.

The crystal-mine key opens the large door to a room with several crystal outcrops in the south-east corner. Use a chisel to cut a piece from the crystal outcrop (35 Crafting). If you forgot your chisel, go back up the lift and pick up the chisel from on top of the crate. You will obtain a salve shard that can be crafted into a new amulet. Be sure to cut extras for backup!
Note: Mining a mithril ore from the veins on the wall within this room will complete a task in the hard Morytania Diary.
A nearby cart tunnel leads right back to the entrance of the mine and can henceforth be used as a shortcut.
Congratulations, quest complete!
Speak with Ceril Carnillean ( of the house south-west of East Ardougne castle) (What's wrong? → Yes.)
Siding with Ceril will reward 5 additional coins and gives you the option to obtain Carnillean armour, although this armour has lower defensive bonuses than an iron platebody.
Siding with Hazeel will reward the Hazeel's mark, which is a purely cosmetic reward.
Turn Valve 1 LEFT
Turn Valve 2 RIGHT
Turn Valve 3 RIGHT
Turn Valve 4 RIGHT
Turn Valve 5 RIGHT
Enter the [[Ardougne Sewers
Board the raft, and talk to Alomone to the south.
Kill Alomone and loot the Carnillean armour from the chest.
(Optional) If you want extra pieces of armour, multiple can be obtained using the drop trick. It can not be reobtained after the quest.
Board the raft again and run back to the Carnilleans house.
Talk to Ceril Carnillean (quest incomplete!)
Search the [[cupboard (Hazeel Cult)
Enter the [[Ardougne Sewers
Turn Valve 1 LEFT
Turn Valve 2 RIGHT
Turn Valve 3 RIGHT
Go to the basement of the Carnilleans house (ladder)
Use the bottle of poison on the cooking range.
Talk to Ceril on the .
Talk to Clivet.
Turn Valve 4 RIGHT
Turn Valve 5 RIGHT
Go back to the cave and board the raft.
Talk to Alomone.
Go back to the Carnilleans' house.
Talk to Butler Jones.
Go in the basement and search the [[crate (Hazeel Cult)
Go up the ladder and stairs and knock on the wall in the east room, and go up the ladder.
Unlock and search the chest to find [[Hazeel scroll
Return to Alomone.
Congratulations, quest complete!

Head to the house in the south-western corner of East Ardougne and speak to Ceril Carnillean, who will start ranting about thieving cultists. Ask him what's wrong, and he'll explain that some cultists have stolen a suit of armour. You will offer to help get the armour back, and Ceril will point you in the direction of a cave to the south of the city. Head east of the clock tower, and enter the cave.
left

At this stage you will have a choice between two sides in this quest: helping Ceril get his family armour back and foiling the plan to revive Hazeel, or helping Hazeel's followers murder a Carnillean and resurrect their master.

The reward is almost the same for either side. Siding with Ceril rewards 5 additional coins, and gives you the option to obtain Carnillean armour, a weak armour with lower defensive bonuses than an iron platebody. This side is quicker, but requires killing Alomone, which is not recommended for very low-level players. Siding with Hazeel will reward the Hazeel's mark, which is a purely cosmetic reward.

Rewards may only be obtained during or upon completion of the quest, and can never be reclaimed afterward. Your choice will also have a minor effect on the events of the quest Secrets of the North. If siding with Ceril, read the following section; if siding with Hazeel, click here to skip to the section below.
Weapon, armour and food

If you've chosen to side with Ceril, talk to Clivet in the cave to learn about Hazeel, an ancient and powerful follower of Zamorak who was killed by an ancestor of Ceril. He will ask for your help in reviving Hazeel. Refuse.
Clivet will sail away on a raft, saying that you'll never be able to find him. Go back upstairs, find the sewer valves, and turn them in the proper direction.
left
Valve 1 - North of the cave. Turn it left.
Valve 2 - West of Valve 1, southern end of the bridge by the Carnilleans' house. Turn it right.
Valve 3 - North-east of Valve 2, across the bridge. Turn it right.
Valve 4 - Other side of the river from Valve 3; cross the bridge again and head east towards the zoo's penguin cage. Turn it right.
Valve 5 - South-east of Valve 4, past the monk. Turn it right.

After you've turned all five, go back into the cave. Board the raft, then head to the southernmost room and talk to Alomone. He will let it slip that Ceril's butler is part of the cult, before attacking you. Kill him, then open the chest in the room to get the Carnillean armour.
Note: You can use the drop trick if you want your own armour.

Board the raft again in order to return to the sewer entrance. Back at the Carnilleans' house, talk to Ceril Carnillean, who will take the armour from you and give you 5 coins. After the player accuses the butler, he will refuse to believe you.
You'll see a quest reward screen, but you haven't received the real reward yet!
Search the cupboard on the and you will find the Mark of Hazeel and a bottle of poison. Show these to Ceril. He will fire Butler Jones and give you the real quest reward.

If you've chosen to side with Hazeel, make sure you have a free inventory slot and then talk to Clivet to learn about Hazeel. He will explain that Hazeel is an ancient and powerful follower of Zamorak who was killed by an ancestor of Ceril. He will ask for your help in reviving Hazeel. Accept.
He wants you to prove your loyalty by killing Ceril. Ask him how, and he will give you some poison and instruct you to pour it in Ceril's food.

Head to the basement of Ceril's house, and use the bottle of poison on the range. Then, go upstairs and talk to Ceril Carnillean to learn that you've accidentally killed Scruffy the family dog instead; his son gave the meal to him.

Talk to Clivet again, and he will have heard about the accident, but takes it as proof of your loyalty regardless. He'll give you Hazeel's mark, then tell you to meet with their leader Alomone in their hideout. To get to the hideout, you need to find five Sewer valves and turn them the proper direction.
Valve 1 - North of the cave. Turn it left.
Valve 2 - West of Valve 1, southern end of the bridge by the Carnilleans' house. Turn it right.
Valve 3 - North-east of Valve 2, across the bridge. Turn it right.
Valve 4 - Other side of the river from Valve 3; cross the bridge again and head east towards the zoo's penguin cage. Turn it right.
Valve 5 - South-east of Valve 4, past the monk. Turn it right.

Go back to the cave and board the raft. Once you're in the main hideout, talk to Alomone. He wants you to help the Carnillean's butler, an undercover cultist, retrieve a magical scroll of restoration that is hidden in the Carnilleans' house.

Talk to Butler Jones in the house, who believes the scroll is hidden where even the family won't find it. Search the crate in the basement for a chest key (make sure to finish the dialogue to get the key in your inventory). Go up the ladder, then up the stairs and knock on the wall in the east room, on the northern side, then finally go up the ladder. Use the key on the chest to get the scroll. Return to Alomone to start Hazeel's resurrection.
Talk to Prince Itzla Arkan at the Teomat to start the quest. ()
Talk to him again after the cutscene.
Travel to the Quetzacalli Gorge (There is a [[Quetzal Transport System
Talk to the bartender in the south-west pub and ask to rent the room for 30 coins. (I'd like to rent the basement room. → I'll take it.)
Enter the south-eastern room in the same building (there is no basement) and rest on the bed.
Talk to the Prince.
Talk to the shopkeeper in the general store east of the pub about help. (I hear you can offer help to those in need.)
Return to the rented room in the pub and talk to the Prince again.

Go through the large gate to the north and run all the way east to the Tower of Ascension and talk to the Prince (Alright, I'll get mingling.) (just outside the entrance to the tower with the dungeon icon on the minimap).
Optionally, build the Unbuilt Landing Site in the Salvager Overlook on your way there if you haven't already done so.
Talk to the nearby recruits, Nova, Sergius, Felius, and Caritta.
Talk to the Prince again (Could you remind me what Ximoua is?) (make sure you don't have a pet following you, or you'll be unable to proceed)
Enter the tower to the west and talk to Forebearer Janus and climb the stairs.
Pickpocket the Emissary Ascended in the caged area on the for a [[Tower key (The Heart of Darkness)
Use the key to open the south-eastern gate, open the chest to receive a [[Book (The Heart of Darkness)
Open the south-western chest with a keyword. The solution is different for each player.
The solution can be found by connecting the first letter of each highlighted word in the book
Read the poem, then talk to Prince Itzla
Open the north-western chest with the code, the code is unique for each person.
Transcribe the marked words from the poem into directions: Takam: East, Makt: North, Silam: West, Uitt: South
Combine the scraps of paper to reveal the passcode.
Speak the passcode to Forebearer Janus on the current floor. Do not go downstairs to speak with him as this will reset the trial.

This is a wave-based combat trial, with melee and mage enemies attacking two at a time, then four at a time. Some of them do a 3x3 AOE attack which can be dodged. Use the [[Bandages (The Heart of Darkness)
Speak to Forebearer Janus again to start the next trial.
Talk to the prince
You must question each member of the cult to work out who the traitor is. Choose the person who mentions anything about [[Ranul
Once you question each one, you'll be given the option to accuse them while talking to them.
If none of the members are the traitor you may need to exit and re-enter the floor.
Go up the stairs.
Fight Prince Itzla.
Pray melee against his basic attacks.

He has two special attacks, both of which he warns you about. The sword swipe turns off any protection prayers, but you can turn them straight back on. The other is an AOE attack, once he warns you he is going to do it, run behind him immediately to dodge.
He is immune to special attacks. (NOTE: If using a Scythe of Vitur; you must unequip it and punch or kick to finish the fight.)
Talk to Forebearer Janus.
Search the chest south to obtain a set of Twilight Emissary robes.
Equip the emissary robes, speak to Prince Itzla to have him follow you, and then enter the temple to the east.
After the cutscene, speak with Prince Itzla and then speak with Forebearer Fides.
Enter the ruins south of the temple and go down the stairs.
Take a pickaxe from the barrel near the entrance.
Mine the rocks.
Run past the Frost Nagua and the spikes and pull the first [[Lever (Ruins of Tapoyauik)
Climb-Down the Ledge, run past the [[frost crab
Throughout the cave, several [[Trap (Ruins of Tapoyauik)
Slide along the icy ledge, and then enter the room in the north-east and pull the second lever.
Continue through the cave and jump over the frozen platforms to get to the west side.
Climb down another ledge, and run into the north-western room with stone chests to pull the third lever
Walk south-west to the large gate and pull the fourth lever located on the northern wall next to the gate. Note: If you forgot a lever, not all braziers will be lit and the gate will be closed.
Pull the chain before continuing, as this will allow you to climb up and down it in the future.
Walk west through the gate and search urns to collect three coloured icons.
Level 104 Frost Nagua will continue to spawn and attack you while searching. Protect from Magic will negate the damage from their regular attacks.
Fix the broken statues in the western area with the corresponding coloured icons.
Inspect the four markings in the four corners of the area. The first word describes the order in which to activate the four statues to open the frozen door.
Different for every player: check the murals and they will have Zema (1), Oma (2), Yeya (3), or Naui (4). Touch the statues in the order determined by the markings (1-4).
Go through the door, prepared to fight the final boss.
Fight the Amoxliatl.
Pray magic
Step away from the spikes
Avoid standing on the ice pools
Re-enable protect from magic when it is disabled
The blocks she summons will deal area damage and heal her, melee them to destroy them. (higher level players can leave these and just attack with fire spells)
Head to the Sunrise Palace and speak to Servius, Teokan of Ralos to finish up the quest.

Start the quest where you left off at the end of Twilight's Promise, at the Teomat. Speak to Prince Itzla, who will propose you and him go undercover by infiltrating the Twilight Emissaries. As he discusses the plan, his mother, Queen Zyanyi Arkan, will arrive. Frustrated at her son's failure to protect his father, Itzla tells her about his plans to lead the infiltration. However, she refuses, insisting that he confide in someone he absolutely trusts to lead in his stead. After the Queen's departure, Itzla relents and asks you to visit a pub in the Quetzacalli Gorge to meet a trusted contact of his, who will fill you in on the infiltration operation.

Head south-west towards Renu and fly to the Quetzacalli Gorge, then head to the Windbreaker pub and speak to the bartender. Ask him to rent the basement room as instructed, only to find out a basement doesn't exist; he will offer to let you rent the ground floor room for 30 coins instead. If you don't have 30 coins, either pickpocket the citizens around the area or use the bank just east of the pub. Once you have the coins, accept the bartender's offer, then head to the east room and rest at the bed.

Upon waking up, you will find a disguised Prince Itzla to be your "trusted contact". He claims that there are very few people he can trust after the events of the previous quest, and that the less people who know about his mission, the better; additionally, as an outsider fairly uninvolved in Varlamorian politics, you ironically are far more trustworthy. He will then tell you that he believes a shopkeeper in the Gorge is recruiting members for the cult, and that you will pose as a potential recruit in the hopes he'll contact the Emissaries.

Head out east to the Quetzacalli Gorge General Store and speak to the shopkeeper, and tell him that you've heard he can offer help to those in need. He is initially skeptical, but accepts your request to join the Emissaries, and tells you and your "friend" to head to the Twilight Temple, where he'll send word for them to expect two recruits. Return to Prince Itzla at the Windbreaker, he will then meet you at the Temple.
4 empty inventory slots

Head north-east past the gate, and make your way east past the Proudspire, then head south to the Tower of Ascension to meet Prince Itzla. He will tell you that a person named Forebearer Janus will call on the both of you when its time to be tested. In the meantime, he wishes to speak to the nearby recruits for insights on why they wish to join the Emissaries.

Talk to the nearby recruits: Nova, Sergius, Felius, and Caritta. Nova will speak of the Augur, the new leader of the Emissaries, who has reorganized the cult and is said to guide them to Mokhaiotl. Return to Prince Itzla, who will explain that Mokhaiotl refers to the centre of the world, which is where it is said Ximoua will happen. As you discuss this with him, Forebearer Janus calls on the both of you to begin your trials.

Before leaving, it is recommended that you bring the materials to build a landing site: 10 quetzal feed, 3 limestone bricks, and 4 soft clay, as you'll be in proximity to the Salvager Overlook landing site en route to the Temple.

You will be in a room with three Emissary Ascended. Pickpocket one of them to obtain a tower key, which is used to open the south-east gate. Search the chest to receive a book and scrap of paper. Take note of the first letter of each white word in the book, which is the passcode for the south-western chest; you will receive a poem and another scrap of paper.

The first word of each verse in the poem uses the language of the Old Ones, translated as cardinal directions: Takam = East, Makt = North, Silam = West, Uitt = South. Reference the poem to get the order of arrows for the code for the last chest located in the north-west part of the room. Enter the code to get the last scrap of paper. Combine the three for a completed note, which contains a pass phrase.
Speak the pass phrase to Forebearer Janus to complete the first trial.
Welcome to your next trial. Here, there is one simple goal... Survive.

The second trial is combat-based, with Emissary Brawlers (melee) and Emissary Conjurers (magic) attacking two at a time, then four at a time. The level 86 brawlers can use a special attack that strikes the tiles adjacent to them, while the conjurers can heal themselves and adjacent brawlers. These special attacks are marked by black shadows appearing on the ground. Players should take care to move out of the brawlers' special attack as it can hit through prayer. The prince is able to dodge this attack on his own.
There are a total of four waves:
Wave 1: Two level 74 brawlers initially, with two reinforcements replacing them as each falls.
Wave 2: One level 74 and one level 86 brawler initially, with two reinforcements of the same kind.
Wave 3: One level 86 brawler and one conjurer initially, which are replaced by one level 74 brawler and another conjurer.
Wave 4: Two level 86 brawlers and two conjurers at the same time, with no reinforcements.

Both you and Prince Itzla must survive the trial; use the bandages from the medical boxes around the room on him to heal. There are a total of three boxes with five bandages each, and will heal 18 hitpoints to Prince Itzla. The bandages can also be used on yourself, but will heal less12 HP from one source, unsure if this scales than when used on the prince. Lower level players who cannot clear the trial quickly should be careful to leave enough to heal him.
If Prince Itzla dies, you will fail the trial and have to restart. The bandage boxes will be refilled.
Speak to Forebearer Janus again to start the third trial. Any remaining bandages should be used to heal before this as they will be removed upon proceeding.

The third trial involves questioning the members of the cult - Tenoch, Silia, Adrius, and Eleuia - and working out who the traitor is. Ask each of them either why they joined the Emissaries or what they know about the Final Dawn; the traitor (different for each player) will always mention Mictl. Mictl (the afterlife in the Losanium religion) not only doesn't exist in the religion of the Twilight Emissaries, but is also in conflict with its cyclic cosmological model, where the world is periodically destroyed and rebuilt into a new one. Once you question each member, you'll be given the option to accuse them while talking to them. If none of the members mention Mictl, you may need to exit and re-enter the floor.
If the chosen member is the traitor, Janus will kill them rather than keep them barely alive; speak to him to begin the final trial.
Victory is within your reach, but one more trial awaits... Face your opponent.

The final trial requires you to battle Prince Itzla. He uses melee attacks, so Protect from Melee is advised. He will use protection prayers whenever you perform a special attack, and uses two in turn, both of which he will warn you about in advance. For instance, he will pray Protect from Magic if a Voidwaker special is used.

The sword swipe special attack turns off any active protection prayers, but you can simply reactivate them without any delay. The other is an AoE attack, once he warns you he is going to do it, run behind him immediately to dodge.
Upon his defeat, speak to Janus to complete the trials.

Now that you and Prince Itzla have passed the trials, the Augur herself will oversee the initiation process. Open the nearby chest to obtain the Twilight Emissary Robes, then wear them and make your way to the Twilight Temple to begin a cutscene.
Note: If you teleport out or walk too far, Itzla will go back to the Tower of Ascension.

During the initation, it is revealed that the Augur is indeed Metzli, the Teokan of Ranul, and claims Ennius and Furia Tullus are the mortal forms of Ralos and Ranul, who were reborn as the twins during an eclipse 31 years ago.

After the cutscene, speak to Forebearer Fides. She will task you with opening up the passage to the Ruins of Tapoyauik, a fortress of the Old Ones under the temple, where Metzli believes they left behind secrets to bring about the Final Dawn. Make your way to the building directly south, and climb down the stairs to the blocked passage; a barrel containing pickaxes can be found nearby to mine it.

Upon mining the blockage, a cutscene will play in which you proceed further into the fortress. However, the ground rumbles, manifesting two frost nagua, killing Forebearer Vulcan and knocking Prince Itzla over a pit.

Note: Once you have completed the cutscene, you no longer need to wear the Twilight Emissary Robes to proceed. The robes will be required in the subsequent quest The Final Dawn, and can be reclaimed at anytime from the chest you found them in.

You will now need to navigate the fortress to meet up with Prince Itzla. Run past the frost nagua (use Protect from Magic if able), then avoid the spear traps; getting hit by one will stun you and deal 6-12 damage. Once past them, pull the lever and climb down the nearby ledge.

Next, run past the frost crabs and make your way north, avoiding stepping on the traps by taking the middle path. You will come across a wall by an icy ledge that you can slide across. Once across, enter the north-eastern room and move around the trap before pulling the lever. Move west to the frozen platforms and cross them, then climb down the western ledge.

Head west to the enclosed room and pull another lever, avoiding the trap. Head south to find a large gate and another lever to pull on the north side. Before entering, pull the chain just east to unlock a shortcut to the exit. If you need to leave and come back, climb down the stairs to enter the dungeon and head west to climb down this chain.
There are four total levers to pull, each lever lighting a brazier at the large gate.

When you walk west through the gate, you will find yourself in a large, rectangular room divided into thirds. The eastern third that you start in contains many urns and two murals. The middle third has a floor of ice and several frost nagua. The western third contains urns, another two murals, four statues, and a frozen door.

Do not search the urns yet - whilst searching urns, frost naguas will spawn and attack and cannot be safespotted. Instead, inspect the two murals and take note of the first words used (zema, oma, yeya, naui) and the corresponding element that is visible on them. You will need to recall these word-element pairs soon. Then, run all the way west to meet up with Prince Itzla. He will help you fight any nagua that you bring near him.
Now in the western third of the room, inspect the other two murals for their words and elements. Check which three of the statues are broken. Then, you will need to run back east again.

In the eastern third again, search the urns to find three distinct icons which correspond to the broken statues that you inspected earlier. The icons will be found in the urns corresponding to their elements, but there are multiple possible urns for each icon. Incorrect urns will spawn a frost nagua that will attack and chase you around the room. Once you have all three icons, run west again.

Finally, in the western third again, use the icons on their corresponding statues. Once you have done so, you will need to touch each of the four statues in the correct order. The words on the murals determine the order in which the player must touch the statues: Zema = 1, Oma = 2, Yeya = 3, and Naui = 4. Meanwhile, the elements on the murals determine the specific statue that must be touched. The order is different for each player. If all statues are touched, but in the incorrect order, you will take damage from falling rocks.

Upon touching the statues correctly, they will unleash a wave spell, melting the ice off the door and killing any remaining frost naguas near it. The next section will be a boss fight, so return to a bank if needed.
Combat gear (Melee combat strongly recommended)

Enter the door to begin a cutscene in which you and Prince Itzla encounter Amoxliatl, a powerful frost nagua guarding the fortress. She will tell you and Itzla that the Mokhaiotl - or the Tlati archive - is off-limits to humans, claiming they are unworthy. Suddenly, Prince Itzla is teleported away, revealing that Metzli, Ennius, and Furia followed you here. As they attempt to deal with you, Amoxliatl claims they have defiled Tapoyauik and will face the consequences. However, as they teleport away, you are forced to fight her in their stead.
The Heart of Darkness - Amoxliatl.png|The player and Prince Itzla encounter Amoxliatl.
The Heart of Darkness - Metzli and the Tullus twins.png|Metzli and the Tullus twins reveal themselves.

The quest version of Amoxliatl is somewhat easier than the regular fight, possessing 400 hitpoints instead of 520 and having more forgiving damage. Nevertheless, players will still have to properly handle her mechanics to beat the fight.

Amoxliatl uses three different attacks. In her standard attack, she attacks with magic, summoning ice spikes on the player's current tile and around the arena. Protect from Magic will protect against the initial attack, but the ice spikes additionally deal typeless damage. Finally, an icy pool will be left on the tile where the player was originally standing that will deal 6-10 damage per tick.

After every 2-4 standard attacks, Amoxliatl will use one of two special attacks. The first one used is randomly selected, but after that, she will alternate between them and will not use the same special attack twice in a row. If you are standing in the narrow entry path, she will not use her Unstable Ice special attack.

Unstable ice blocks: Amoxliatl forms 1-4 blocks of unstable ice around the arena. If not destroyed in time (16 ticks, ~10 seconds), all remaining ice blocks will shatter, causing icy pools to form within 3x3 of the ice blocks and healing the boss (16-25) for each ice block shattered. The ice blocks can only be destroyed with melee, and melee attacks against them will result in a max hit with an attack speed of 1.

Icicle attack: Amoxliatl disables the player's prayer and launches an icicle at them. A message is shown in the chatbox: Amoxliatl disables your prayers and launches an icicle attack! Turn on Protect from Magic before the icicle hits you to negate all damage.

After defeating Amoxliatl, you will forcefully be banished from Tapoyauik. Make your way to Sunrise Palace, where Servius is currently staying. You will inform him of the events that transpired, and he will ask that you leave so as to avoid the Queen's anger, but assures you that you will be involved in whatever plans are made next.
Congratulations, quest complete!
Talk to Achietties outside the Heroes' Guild in Burthorpe. (I'm a hero, may I apply to join? → I'll start looking for all those things then.)
Talk to Gerrant, the fishing shop owner in Port Sarim about lava eels. (I want to find out how to catch a lava eel.) He'll give you a bottle of blamish snail slime.
Use the blamish snail slime on your harralander potion (unf) to create blamish oil.
Buy a fishing rod and some bait if you do not have them.
Right-click to use the oil on your fishing rod.
Travel to the Taverley Dungeon.
You can visit the Wilderness Lava Maze to obtain the eel, but it is advised against due to its location unless you want to also complete the hard Wilderness Diary task.

Alternatively, players with 60 Sailing (non boostable) can go to the Charred Dungeon located at the Charred Island, the route is closer and doesn't require agility nor a key like Taverley Dungeon does but players will need to pass throught a bunch of lava Strykewyrms.
To obtain a dusty key:
Use the map (pictured right) to find Velrak the explorer. He is in the southern part of the dungeon.
Kill the Jailer standing by the prison and use the key he drops to get into Velrak's cell.
Talk to him for the dusty key. (So do you know any good places to explore? → Yes please!) Do not ask for a reward.
Enter the area with the blue dragons, either by using your key on the locked door or take the agility shortcut.
Run to the southernmost lava pool.
Catch a lava eel. You only need one, as they cannot be burned. (Catch extra in case you accidentally eat it.)
Cook the eel on a range or fire.
To obtain the ice gloves:
Equip combat gear and food to kill a level 111 Ice Queen.
Go to White Wolf Mountain. Note: If you need to boost your mining to 50, bring the boost with you.
Walk to the northern part of the mountain, mine the rockslide.
Take the southern ladder.
Follow the tunnel south, go up the ladder.
Take the eastern ladder down.
Go through the long tunnel.
Go up the ladder.
Go down the northern ladder. Run north and kill the queen for her gloves.
Equip the ice gloves.
Travel to Entrana.
Kill the Firebird near the Law Altar, take the fire feather.
Take the feather, eel, and armband to Achietties.
Congratulations, quest complete!
Throne of Miscellania
Legends' Quest
Recipe for Disaster
The Fremennik Exiles

full.h: The greatest heroes of the land

steps.t: Talk to Achietties outside the Heroes' Guild just south of Burthorpe about joining the guild. If you meet the requirements, she will acknowledge your questing prowess and set you the entry tasks. She will tell you that in order to get in you need to give her three items: a fire feather from an Entrana firebird, a cooked lava eel, and a Master Thieves' Armband.

For the armband, she suggests you probably have 'relevant contacts' yourself with whom to enquire about it. To obtain the feather she only offers the most helpful advice that Entranan firebirds tend to live on Entrana. To get the eel, she advises you to talk to someone who knows a lot about fishing.
The items may be obtained in any order, but must be given to Achietties simultaneously.

To earn the armband, you will have to contact your old gang associates from the Shield of Arrav quest, as indicated by the quest journal. For this part of the quest, you will need the help of a player of the opposite gang. Players that have completed the quest may go back and help others. For finding a quest partner, the Grouping interface is useful. You can also usually find a partner on the chat-channel 'Osrs Soa' during peak hours.

Note: For this part of the quest you do not need to meet the skill requirements. This means you can complete this part of the quest in order to help a friend complete their entire quest; see Trivia for more details. You can even help a friend if you have already completed the quest yourself.

Note: Traded Pete's candlesticks will not be accepted if the presenter did not kill Grip. As such, do not get scammed into buying or taking free candlesticks unless you are a Phoenix Gang member and can kill Grip. Black Arm gang members can never kill Grip so they should not accept traded candlesticks under any circumstances. Likewise, a miscellaneous key without a Black Arm member to lure Grip is useless. Do not get scammed into buying miscellaneous keys.
A black full helm, a black platebody and black platelegs

Go to Varrock and talk to Katrine who is inside the Black Arm Gang Headquarters, which is situated in the south-west of the city. She tells you that you need to do something amazing in order to attain the rank of master thief. She explains some of the most coveted items for thieves are in Brimhaven. The leader of the pirates there is one Scarface Pete. She will tell you that you have to steal his very valuable candlesticks and that his security is very good.
You have to visit the Black Arm members in their hideout in the alleyway of Palm Street. The gang's password is "four leafed clover".

Go to Brimhaven and find the gang office, which is the building along the fence, east of the two inns and south of the Agility Arena. Give Grubor the password "four leaved clover" at the door, and inside speak to Trobert, the leader of the Black Arms in Brimhaven. Trobert explains one of the only keys to Pete's treasure room is carried by his head guard Grip, who was taking on a new deputy called Hartigen, a deserter of the Black Knights seeking employment in Brimhaven. The Black Arms have waylaid Hartigen and stolen his identification papers. Volunteer to impersonate Hartigen. He will give you the Id papers, which you will need to get into Scarface Pete's mansion, and tell you to introduce yourself to its guards.

Speak to Garv, who is the guard patrolling along the southern wall of the large building on Brimhaven's western side. He will not believe you are Hartigen, stating that the Black Knight dressed differently. Equip a full set of black armour: full helm, platebody and platelegs. Garv will then allow you to go inside tells you to speak to Grip.

full.h: Getting a Grip on the key

steps.t: Once inside, talk to Grip. He explains you will be working various guard duties, and that the important keys are in Grip's jacket. Ask him "So what do my duties involve?" and then "Anything I can do now?" and he will give you a Miscellaneous key.
Note: If you have already done the quest and have the Miscellaneous key in your bank, he will not give you a new one.

Grip won't allow you to enter the treasure room and you can't kill him without drawing attention to yourself. This means you will need an accomplice. Leave the building and trade the key to your Phoenix Gang partner.

Back inside, head into the north-eastern room from the entrance. Wait for your partner to get to the room behind the eastern wall, behind the arrowslit; then, search the cupboard. A pirate guard will say that Grip really doesn't like his drinks cabinet being touched, but open it anyway. Grip will then come into the room, telling you to get your hands off his drinks. Make sure the door is open. Grip can become stuck on the guards in the room, so you may need to wait or kill some guards to create space or else Grip may be blocked and leave the room. If this happens, just search the cupboard again. It's common for Grip to not come in the room all the way or retreat after being hit, so closing the door after he enters helps.
Your Phoenix Gang partner will then kill Grip through the slit from the hidden room. Once he dies, pick up Grip's keyring.

Using the key, go to the treasure room (the room with coins on the floor next to the staircase in the north-west corner) and open the north chest in the first room to receive two candlesticks. Give one candlestick to your Phoenix Gang partner.
Go back to Varrock and talk to Katrine. She will give you the Thieves' armband.
Note: The door to the treasure room will not open and give you a message if you attempt to open it with Grip's keyring without having obtained a miscellaneous key at least once.

Note: The chest containing Pete's candlesticks (position to the north) will be empty if you have a candlestick in your inventory or bank. If you have a traded one in the bank, you will need to discard it then come back to search this chest as you will not be able to turn in a traded candlestick to Katrine at any time.
Note: Be sure to pick up the candlesticks yourself; otherwise, Katrine will say you weren't the one to retrieve the candlestick and you will have to go back to do it all over again.
