Romeo can be found in or near Varrock Square. Speak to him, and he'll ramble about his love for Juliet. Ask him if you can help, and he'll ask you to talk to her in her mansion.

Go and talk to Juliet, located on the upper floor balcony of the mansion directly west of the Varrock west bank, just outside the western walls of Varrock. She will give you a letter to give to Romeo. Go back to Romeo at Varrock Square, and deliver the letter. If you cannot find Romeo, he may have wandered inside the general store located south of the square.

After delivering the letter to Romeo, he will despair upon learning that Juliet's father opposes their marriage. He suggests going to Father Lawrence for help, who is located in the Varrock church north-east of the square. After speaking to Father Lawrence, he will suggest that you fake Juliet's death by giving her a cadava potion to appear dead, so that Romeo can later collect her from the crypt. He will ask you to go to the Apothecary who will be able to make one for you.

Note: You can save some time by having the cadava berries required for the potion in your inventory before speaking to the apothecary. Consider also picking one extra for the quest Making Friends with My Arm. Ironman players are recommended to grab some redberries at the same time as the cadava berries, for use in later quests.

The Apothecary can be found in south-western Varrock located west of the Varrock Swordshop, in a building with a purple potion icon. Speak to him about the quest (selecting 'Talk about something else' first) and he will ask you to bring him some cadava berries to finish the potion.

Cadava berries can be picked from several bushes just west of the south-east Varrock mine. Return to the Apothecary with the berries and he will give you the cadava potion. Be careful not to drink the potion yourself, as this will cause the player to black out for a short amount of time.

Go back to Romeo, and tell him that he must rescue Juliet from the crypt. He needs someone to accompany him, which ends up being you. You will now see another cutscene of you entering the crypt with Romeo. When he sees Juliet's cousin, Phillipa, he forgets all about Juliet and falls in love with her.
Congratulations, quest complete!
Head to Tirannwn (Catherby teleport (tablet), use charter to Port Tyras)
Track down Islwyn, who will be either west of Lletya or north-east of the Tyras Camp. Use [[:File:Isafdar map.png
Offer your help to Islwyn. (Tell the truth? → Maybe I could help.)
Talk to Eluned.
Bank all your combat equipment, runes included.
Go to Tree Gnome Village dungeon and retrieve Glarial's pebble if you didn't save one from Waterfall Quest.
Travel north-west of the Fishing Guild and use Glarial's pebble on Glarial's tombstone.
Kill a Moss Guardian (level 84). It will drop a consecration seed.
Take the seed to Eluned.
Enter the Waterfall Dungeon.
Board the log raft north of Baxtorian Falls.
Use a rope on the rock.
Use a rope on the dead tree.
Open the door to enter.
(Skip this step if you already have the [[A key (Waterfall Dungeon)
Take the west path all the way north.
Left click the seed in the final room to plant it.
Return to Islwyn to choose your reward.
Congratulations, quest complete!
Optional: Speak to Eluned to start Mourning's End Part I, which will allow you to receive the teleport crystal to Lletya.
Mourning's End Part I

Talk to Islwyn to start the quest. He will be found with his companion Eluned in one of two locations in Isafdar. Refer to the map for the possible locations and the routes towards them. Head towards either of these spots; if he isn't there, switch to another world until you find him. These elven woods may be reached by travelling with a charter ship (Port Tyras), using an Iorwerth camp teleport or by traversing through the Underground Pass or by using the overpass of Arandar.
Note that travelling through Isafdar can be rather dangerous due to the vast amount of traps, that deal up to 15 damage at once and may apply poison. Food and antipoison are recommended.

After the events of Regicide, the player decides to help the rebelling elves, led by Arianwyn, against Lord Iorwerth's apparent scheme to take over Camelot. Arianwyn sent out scouts, Islwyn and Eluned, to guide you to their holdout. However, Islwyn seemingly distrusts any human and will not assist you, as it was an act of humans that led to his grandmother's death. He will mention that his grandmother was Glarial, whose remains you moved from her tomb to the Waterfall Dungeon during the Waterfall Quest. He will be surprised and relieved upon hearing this, as he believes this to be the perfect resting place for her.

Islwyn changes his mind and will help you, on the condition you complete the ritual of burying her. Speak with Eluned to learn about this ritual. She will tell you to retrieve the consecration seed from her previous resting place. Talk to Eluned before leaving for the tomb or you will not be able to retrieve the seed.
You will require Glarial's pebble to enter the tomb. If you have lost this, speak with Golrie in the Tree Gnome Village Dungeon to obtain another.
Glarial's pebble
Having talked with Eluned, head towards Glarial's Tomb and use the pebble to enter it. Note that there will be many restrictions to entering the tomb.

You will need to kill any level-84 Moss Guardian to retrieve the consecration seed. Because of the restrictions towards entering the tomb, the simplest way to fight it is using unarmed melee. See the list of exceptions for alternatives, including Magic. Prayer, food, and potions may be used and it is advised to do so. As the Moss Guardian does physical damage, or unavoidable magical damage if the physical damage doesn't land, it is recommended to pray Protect from Melee. The ring of recoil will also prove effective. You can wield the goblin paint cannon to increase your attack speed, as it isn't restricted. You can wear H.A.M. clothing for a little extra defence bonus. It is also possible to flinch it by standing directly south of the south-eastern pillar when fighting the Moss Guardian directly west of the entrance.

Take the consecration seed back to Eluned, who has possibly moved to the other location shown on the map. If she has moved, you can switch worlds until she appears. She will enchant the seed by casting a silent spell on it. If you lose the seed after this point, you may return to her for a new one.
Glarial's amulet,Rope, Spade, [[Key (Waterfall Dungeon)

Travel to the Waterfall Dungeon with all the required items. Similar to how you entered it during the Waterfall Quest, board the raft in the middle of the lake above the Baxtorian Falls. It will crash just before the waterfall. Then, use the rope on the rock to the south, followed by using the rope once again on the dead tree hanging on the edge. You will then find yourself in front of the dungeon entrance.

Inside the dungeon, search the northernmost crates in the eastern room to find a key. With this key, open the locked doors in the western rooms, and proceed to the room with the Chalice of Eternity. Bury the seed anywhere next to the chalice to complete the ritual, laying Glarial's spirit to rest.

Head back to Islwyn to claim your reward. You will be given a choice between a free, but partly used, crystal shield or crystal bow. Both can be bought later from him, for and coins respectively. These items have charges that deplete when using them, after which they will become unusable until recharged by Ilfeen, for a varying cost.
You will need the crystal bow for the Hard Western Provinces Diary. Therefore, in addition to its higher cost, it is advised to take the bow.

If you have the requirements to start Mourning's End Part I, it's highly recommended to speak to Eluned after claiming your reward in order to start the quest. By doing so, Eluned will teleport you to Arianwyn in Lletya, while also granting you a teleport crystal with 4 charges that can be used to teleport there (and Prifddinas upon completion of the Song of the Elves quest). Eluned may have moved locations during the prior dialogue; in this case just switch worlds until she reappears.
Congratulations, quest complete!
Speak to Advisor Ghrim. (Has anything been happening in the kingdom recently? → Very well, I'll sort it out.) (fairy ring code cip)
Talk to Princess Astrid or Prince Brand (depending on who you married), watch the cutscene.
Talk to King Vargas. (Right away, your Majesty.)
Talk to Gardener Gunnhild by the flax patch next to the castle entrance.
Talk to Queen Sigrid. (Of course, it's my duty.)
Talk to Matilda in/around the southern building inside the castle's walls.
Talk to Queen Sigrid. (I suppose so...)

Now is a good time to gear up at the bank at the north part of Etceteria as you won't be coming back here until after the boss fight. Don't forget to take an antipoison to help with the fight. Also take 5 coal or have at least 5 empty spaces. Note: Do not waste time trying to mine coal near Miner Magnus, as you don't actually get any resources. An area to mine coal is provided later on in the quest.
Talk to King Vargas.
Talk to Advisor Ghrim. (King Vargas asked me to talk to you.)
Talk to the Sailor at the Miscellania docks. (I'm looking for a sailor...)
Talk to King Vargas with one open inventory slot to receive a scroll proving you are Regent of Miscellania.
Enter the dungeon, down the ladder in the courtyard (along the castle's south wall).
Talk to Donal in the pub. (Of course. Dealing with monsters is what I do best!)
Go north, take a pick (on the rock next to the dwarves) if you need coal.
Use the mining prop on the [[Crevice (Miscellania Dungeon)
Take an engine and put the 5 coal in it.
Take the following from the crates:
2 beams.
3 pulley beams.
1 rope.
Use a beam on a pulley beam to get a long pulley beam; use another regular beam on it to make a longer pulley beam.
To the broken scaffold add:
A pulley beam.
A longer pulley beam.
A pulley beam.
A rope.
Take:
1 beam.
1 rope.
Add a beam to the platform.
Put the engine on the engine platform.
If you haven't yet, add your five coal to the engine.
Use the lift and take the plank.
Enter the [[Tunnel (Miscellania Dungeon)
Keep running and make sure to continue through your character's dialogue.
Take the diary from the fire remains.
Use your plank to cross the rocks, be sure to collect all diary pages by searching the four additional fires through the cave.
Continue running and avoid the steam vents as they will damage you.
Read the diary and continue through the crevice, watch the cutscene.
Talk to Armod.
Follow the passage north and enter the crevice at the end of the passage
Kill the Giant Sea Snake. Use protect from ranged prayer and attack at a distance (magic preferred).
Take the heavy box.
Leave the crevice of the boss room and climb up the rope for a shortcut back to Etceteria castle.
Talk to Queen Sigrid to receive a letter and 20000 gold. (You need two free inventory slots.)
Talk to King Vargas.

Travel to Miscellania (fairy ring: CIP), and speak to Advisor Ghrim in the castle to start the quest. He'll say that since you took up the position of regent, King Vargas has grown bored and both he and Queen Sigrid have begun threatening each other with another war.

Speak to Prince Brand or Princess Astrid, found in either of the two rooms next to the throne room, and a cutscene will follow. Prince Brand suggests that you convince the King and Queen Sigrid to marry to prevent further catastrophe, which Princess Astrid excitedly agrees upon.
Speak to the King. He'll say that several items from many of Miscellania's citizens have been going missing, and that you should investigate.

Find and speak with either Gunnhild by the herbs, Leif by the trees, Frodi on the dock, or Magnus by the mines (they will all say the same thing, you only need to talk to one of them). Apparently, Etceterian soldiers came to ask for tithes, the workers refused, and the next day items were stolen.
Talk with the King again. He'll send you to discuss this situation with Queen Sigrid.
Speak with Queen Sigrid in Etceteria. She'll tell you to talk to her citizens about things gone missing, criticising the king whenever she gets the chance.
Go downstairs to speak to one of the Etceterian citizens such as Helga, Haming, or Matilda. They will tell you the same story as the workers in Miscellania, only with the roles reversed.

Speak again with Queen Sigrid and update her on the known information. Soldiers have been mentioned in both stories, yet neither side has an army. She'll say this is your responsibility due to your position as regent and demand you solve things.

Note: Be sure to have the things you will need for the fight at this point, utilising the bank directly north on Etceteria. Remember to take antipoison potions and prayer potions as needed. It is recommended to leave about 10 inventory spaces open for items you're going to use later on during the quest.
Go back to Miscellania and speak with King Vargas to review your conversation with the Queen. He'll ask you to speak with Ghrim about the presence of these alleged armies and the missing goods.
Ghrim, assuming these happenings are being caused by outsiders, will suggest you speak with the Sailor at the docks to find out if he's seen any suspicious characters.
Head to the Sailor at the docks of Miscellania. He will mention a group of children who came to the island recently, saying they had gone to go visit their family in the dungeon.
The dungeon is still inaccessible at this point, so speak again with King Vargas to gain access. He'll give you a scroll with his signature.
Take the scroll and enter the dungeon within Miscellania's castle walls (look for the dungeon icon on the minimap), and you will arrive in a small underground settlement.
Go to the pub and speak with a dwarf called Donal.
Head up north, and you will see two dwarf miners. Pick up a bronze pickaxe from the rock if you need one.
Use the mining prop on the crevice and squeeze through it.
Now, you need to repair the lift using items found in the boxes in the chamber:
First, take an engine and three beams, three pulley beams, and two ropes from the crates.

Before you start assembling the whole structure, add five chunks of coal to the engine (this can also be done last, after step 8). If you did not bring coal with you, the chamber has four coal rocks as well as a pickaxe near the dwarves if you forgot one.
Use a pulley beam on the broken scaffold on the east side of the room to attach it.
Use a beam on a pulley beam to make a long pulley beam, and then use it with another beam to get a longer pulley beam, which you must then attach to the scaffold.
Use the final pulley beam on the scaffold.
Use a rope on the scaffold to wind it through the pulleys.
Use the third beam on the platform to repair it.
Place the engine on the engine platform (Note: the engine platform is not the same as the platform from step 7. Rather, it is the one on the tile which faces the engine spawning spot).
Add the 5 pieces of coal to the engine (only necessary if not already added).

The lift should be operational now. While making sure you have another rope, click the 'Use-Lift' option on the platform to head closer to the mysteries of the island. (If this option doesn't appear, make sure you have added 5 coal to the engine. You can do it when placed on the engine platform.)
Take the plank and enter the small tunnel on the east wall. Continue travelling east and use a rope with the overhanging rock to swing across the water.
You will come across the remains of a fire, search it to get the first part of a burnt diary. Read the diary, and save it for later.

Use the plank to cross the slippery rocks - otherwise, you may be hit for 8 damage. The plank is not left behind and may be reused every time. The rocks can also be safely skipped without a plank via the run trick.

As you proceed further into the caves, you will come across two more fire remains, search them to get the second and third part of the diary. After the third fire remains, there will be some steam vents in the ground. Do not walk across or stand on them as they repeatedly damage you depending on your Hitpoints level.

After the vents, there will be another set of fire remains, search it for the fourth part of the diary. Going further down into the caves, there will be some rocks lying on the cliffs above your path. Do not stand or walk under those rocks as they will fall down on you and deal some damage depending on your Hitpoints level.

After progressing through the area with the rocks, you will come across yet another fire remains. Search it to find the fifth and final page for the diary. Once you have completed the diary, you must read it before being able to enter a crevice at the end of the passage.

Enter through the crevice, and you should see a cutscene involving some lost kids. Speak to them to get the full story. The kids had apparently not been able to pass the trials to become a Fremennik, so they were going to start a war here and then stop it, and be seen as heroes. They are to blame for everything.

Travel out through the next exit, and roam the passages where there are lots of Sea Snake Young until you reach another crevice; squeeze through and kill the Giant Sea Snake (level 149, with only 100 HP).

Protect from Melee works fine if you want to run up close. From a distance the snake uses ranged attacks so use Protect from Missiles if ranging or maging. Level 60 Magic and Iban blast will be enough to kill the snake quickly. A Dwarf multicannon can be setup in the boss room to help lower levels defeat the Giant Sea Snake.

Its poison damage hits 9 so an antipoison is strongly recommended. Note that a superantipoison will also negate any effects for 5 minutes. A player who has around level 70 Ranged, full Black d'hide, a Magic Shortbow (i), and Rune arrows, for example, should only need 1 dose of normal Antipoison to kill the Snake. Similarly, level ~70 Melee stats with a Dragon scimitar should also only need 1 dose of antipoison. After the fight, it is also recommended to immediately drink your antipoison because the damage of the poison is very slow, yet heavy.
Pick up the heavy box that the snake drops. If you forget to collect the box before leaving, speak to the guard outside the dungeon on Etceteria.
Return through the crevice. A guard will notice you and help you up, and you will surface near Sigrid's castle.
Go to Queen Sigrid and talk to her. She'll be impressed with you, and she'll give you 20,000 coins as a reward and a letter to take to King Vargas (reading it will not affect the quest).
Talk to King Vargas to give him the letter for the rest of your reward.
Congratulations, quest complete!
Talk to Talia, twice, in the camp just south-west of the Edgeville Monastery.
Talk to Gertrude in her house west of Varrock, just south of the Cooks' Guild.
Interact with the stray dog just south of the western Varrock bank, barking at a [[Guard (Varrock)
Follow the stray dog to the house just west of the [[Thessalia's Fine Clothes.
Inspect the torn newspaper, chewed box, and rough bedding.
Follow the dog again until a cutscene triggers just north of the Cooks' Guild.
Interact with the dog again to ensure the dog is following you, then talk to Picklenose to the south-west of the guild.
You must not have a pet out while the dog is following you.
If you teleport away, the stray dog and her puppy will be waiting near Picklenose or at the den north of the Apothecary.
Use Grain (found north of Cooking Guild) on some fur with a needle and thread (or a costume needle) in your inventory to create a stuffed dog.
Talk to Picklenose again.
Pick up the stray puppy next to the stray dog.
Interact with the stray dog and follow her until another cutscene triggers by the gap in the wall north of the Cooks' Guild.
Kill both outlaws (level 22 and 23) and watch the next cutscene.
Congratulations, quest complete!

Talk to Talia in the camp just south-west of the Edgeville Monastery. The camp can be reached quickly by combat bracelet or skull sceptre teleport. Talia will explain that the monks let them set up a shelter there, but they're struggling to find stray dogs to take in. She'll also explain that they once had cats at the shelter too, later getting help with them from Gertrude. She'll ask you to help bring in the strays, and see if Gertrude can point you in the right direction.

Make your way to Gertrude's house just south of the Cooks' Guild in western Varrock and talk to her. The skills necklace Cooking Guild teleport is quite close to the location. After you mention that Talia's shelter is only caring for dogs now, she'll comment on the "mangy dogs" in Varrock. After defending the dogs, saying they need love too, Gertrude will mention a dog near the bank. Head slightly north-east, and interact with the stray dog just south of the Varrock west bank, which will be barking at a guard.

The guard will mention that the dog is usually quite friendly, but that she's been away for a few weeks. You'll mention that the dog seems persistent, prompting the guard to suggest you follow her. After the dialogue ends, follow the stray dog to the house just west of the clothes shop. Once she arrives, inspect the torn newspaper, chewed box, and rough bedding. You'll realize that the stray's puppies are missing, prompting the dog to start running again.

Follow the dog once more as it runs through the bank, causing a banker to try shooing it out. This time, the dog will stop just north of the Cooks' Guild, where a cutscene will play showing Picklenose trying to catch one of the puppies. After seeing the stray dog, which is much larger than the puppies, he'll flee the area.

After finishing the dialogue with the dog, interact with the dog again to ensure she's following you. Then, run to the west side of the Cooks' Guild and talk to Picklenose, standing amongst several other goblins.
Note: you must not have a pet out while the dog is following you. If you teleport away, the stray and her puppy will be waiting near Picklenose, or at the den north of the Apothecary.

Picklenose will reveal that the goblins plan to train the puppies to become guard dogs for Goblin Village once they're grown. However, it quickly becomes apparent that the goblins have no clue how to properly care for dogs. Your character will instead suggest a stuffed dog, which requires no maintenance. Use the grain on some fur with a needle and thread (or a costume needle) in your inventory to create a stuffed dog. Grain can be picked just north of the Cooks' Guild, if needed. Talk to Picklenose again. The goblins will love the dog, and agree to hand over the puppy.

The stray dog will indicate that there's still one more puppy to find. Interact again, then follow the stray dog. It will go back and forth a few times before finally ending up at the entrance to the outlaw camp, triggering a cutscene. You must now kill two outlaws, level 22 and 23.
After the outlaws have been killed, a final cutscene will play where you bring the puppies back to the shelter, which will now be in business.
Congratulations, quest complete!
Take a rake and a seed dibber from the leprechaun if you haven't got one already.
Talk to Pirate Pete on the dock north-east of the Ectofuntus, decline the money. (Yes! → Of course, I fear no demon! → Nonsense! Keep the money!)
Finish talking to Captain Braindeath. Make sure you have at least one inventory space available to get the Blindweed seed (don't cancel the dialogue after the cutscene).
If you still do not have a rake and a seed dibber, go down the ladder in the north-west corner. Head south-east past the spiders, and search the [[Cupboard (Rum Deal)
Leave the building to the south, down the stairs.
Go south past the zombies and plant the blindweed in the south-eastern-most patch.

Wait about 5 minutes (or a few seconds) for it to grow. (Warning: Nearby Zombie swabs can attack low and mid-levelled players. You can simply log out while waiting.) You'll receive an in-game message when it finishes growing. Pick the plant.
Talk to Captain Braindeath.
Climb-up the ladder in the south-east corner of the big room.
Put the blindweed in the hopper (next to the pressure barrel) in the north-west corner of the room.
Talk to Captain Braindeath. You will automatically get a bucket in your inventory if you don't have one.
Leave the building using the stairs to the south, head west to the bridge, and open the gate north of 50% Luke.
Head north to the water source on the map, and fill the bucket with stagnant water.
Return to the brewery and add the stagnant water to the hopper. (Ectophial and talking to Pirate Pete is faster than walking back.)
Talk to Captain Braindeath.
Fish 5 sluglings. Fishing spots can be found east, south-east, and west of the farming patch. (Note: do not untangle the Fishbowl and net, if you do then use one on the other to retangle.)
Put the sluglings in the pressure barrel by the hopper.
Pull the lever.
Talk to Captain Braindeath.
Talk to Davey in the room to the west, with all the bunk beds. (Note: He will only bless the wrench if you have 47 or more Prayer points)
Use the holy wrench on the shaking brewing control.
Kill the level 150 Evil spirit. (Can be safespotted)
Talk to Captain Braindeath. (Complete the dialogue or the fever spider corpse won't drop)
Climb down the nearby ladder.
Kill a fever spider (can be safespotted by standing north-west of the ladder)
Put its body in the hopper on the top floor.
Talk to Captain Braindeath.
Collect some 'Unsanitary Swill' from the output tap (south end of the brewing machine) using the bucket used for the stagnant water. (if you dropped the first one, he will give you a second one here)
Give it to Captain Donnie outside, amongst the protesters.
Talk to Captain Braindeath.
Congratulations, quest complete!
Cabin Fever

Talk to Pirate Pete at the dock north-east of the Ectofuntus to start the quest. Pirate Pete claims to be a dispossessed nobleman who needs to reclaim his family sword in order to defeat his evil half-brother, who has stolen his lands and is now terrorizing the local lemon farmers. Agree to help him, after which he will warn you about his brother's dangerous ally, the demon Barrelor the Destroyer. Agree nonetheless; Pete will explain his half-brother has stolen most of his fortune, but he will gladly part with what remains for your help. Refuse the money he offers you. He will instruct you to pick up a diversion, knock you out and row you to a secret location.

A cutscene ensues in which Pete delivers you, tied up and unconscious, to a worried pirate captain, revealing that the entire story was fabricated. Upon awakening, you will find yourself in a small room with the captain, who will explain that you are in the brewery on the secret Braindeath Island. He introduces himself as Captain Braindeath, and explains that a week ago the island came under siege of a group of zombie pirates protesting. He needs to make some 'rum' in order to get the protesters' leader Captain Donnie drunk, after which Braindeath and his brewers can sneak out of the factory and set up a new brewery elsewhere. You will have to gather the ingredients to make the rum.

Braindeath will give you a seed in order to grow the first ingredient, blindweed. He explains the zombie swabs have trashed the previous blindweed patches, but that intimidation should be sufficient to get rid of them.

If you don't have the rake and seed dibber yet, go down the ladder in the north-west corner of the building to the basement, and then head south-east past the spiders to find a cupboard. There, take the rake and seed dibber from the cupboard.

Leave the building by the southernmost stairway, towards the farming patches. You may be attacked by zombie swabs; walk out of combat and right-click to "Intimidate" them, which permanently stops them from attacking you. A picture of a kitten will be shown to censor your insults.

The only usable farming patch is the south-eastern one. Use your rake on the patch to remove the weeds and then plant the seed (requires 40 Farming). Note: If you have grabbed more then one seed by drop trick this will plant all of them in the stack, once planted you will be unable to get more. Wait a few minutes for the blindweed to grow; you will receive the notification "I wonder how my blindweed is coming along...". Harvest the crop. Note: Should you lose the blindweed after this, Braindeath will give you some he had in storage all along.

Return to Captain Braindeath, who will tell you to put the blindweed in the hopper upstairs. Use the south-eastern ladder to climb upstairs and then use the blindweed on the hopper in the north-western corner of the room. You can ignore the lever for now. Talk to Captain Braindeath for the next ingredient; stagnant water.
Bucket.
Braindeath will hand you a bucket unless you already have one. You will have to travel to a nearby volcano and fill the bucket with the stagnant water.

Leave the house via the south stairway again and exit the outside fence, then travel north-west to find 50% Luke guarding a small gate (you may equip the Ring of Charos(a) or use a tinderbox on him for some amusing dialogue). Pass the gate behind him and travel up the volcano to collect the stagnant water. Return to the house, pour the water into the hopper, and talk to Captain Braindeath.

Braindeath will give you a fishbowl tangled in a big net. Note: If you untangle the fishbowl and net, you have to use them on each other to re-tangle them. Head to the fishing spots near the farming patch you used earlier. You have to catch a total of FIVE (5) sluglings or karamthulhu and add them to the pressure barrel upstairs in the building, next to the hopper. Pull the lever, and the brewing control apparatus downstairs will start to spin and shake uncontrollably. Return to Captain Braindeath.

The captain will tell you that the controls for the brewery have become possessed, which "occasionally happens". He will give you a wrench in order to beat the controls with it, but remarks that it requires a blessing first for the possessing spirit to come out. Head to the west side of the house and get your wrench blessed by former priest Davey. He will only bless the wrench if you have 47 or more available prayer points. Note that this does not drain any prayer points.

Now, beat up the controls with the holy wrench. They are located directly south of Captain Braindeath. As soon as you hit the controls, a level 150 Evil spirit will appear and attack you. His attacks can be negated with Protect from Melee, or by using a safespot with Ranged, Magic, or a halberd.

Having defeated the evil spirit, Captain Braindeath will tell you that the final ingredient is the carcass of a diseased fever spider. You must complete the dialogue with him or the carcass will not drop!

Go down the nearby ladder into the basement and kill a fever spider. Be warned that fever spiders inflict disease on hit, even with Protect from Melee; you can circumvent this by using a safespot or having slayer gloves equipped, or using a cure such as Relicym's balm. Collect its carcass, use it on the hopper, and return to Captain Braindeath.
Note that killing the fever spider completes a medium Morytania Diary task.
Note: Disease is cured upon completing the quest.

Now that the 'rum' is complete, collect some with a bucket from the output tap at the south end of the machinery. Braindeath gives you a bucket if you don't already have one.

Head outside and find Captain Donnie near the farming patches to give him the unsanitary swill. He will smell the 'rum' and demand you hand it over, downing it as quickly as possible. He will then accidentally disclose the name of his boss, Rabid Jack. Return to Captain Braindeath to inform him of this. He will be shocked at Jack's name before pretending he had never heard of it before. He then thanks you for your help and announces the brewery is not going to be relocated, and they will keep the zombies too drunk to be a bother.
Congratulations, quest complete!
Ask Duke Horacio in Lumbridge Castle for a quest and he'll give you an air talisman. (Have you any quests for me? → Yes.)
Talk to Archmage Sedridor in the Wizards' Tower basement and give him the air talisman. (Okay, here you are. → Actually, I'm not interested. → Yes, certainly.)
Talk to Aubury south of Varrock east bank in the Varrock rune shop and give him the research package. (I've been sent here with a package for you.)
Take the [[Research notes (Rune Mysteries)
Congratulations, quest complete!

Talk to Duke Horacio on the of Lumbridge Castle, and ask if he has any quests to give out. He will explain that although he himself has no tasks for the player, he did find a strange talisman. Curious about its origin, he will give you an air talisman and ask you to bring it to the arch mage of the Wizards' Tower.
Tip: Multiple air talismans can be obtained by using the drop trick at Duke Horacio. This may be useful for early runecraft training methods. For details, see this guide.

Go to the Wizards' Tower found south of Draynor Village, and descend the ladder into the basement to talk to Archmage Sedridor. He will take your air talisman and give you a research package to deliver to Aubury in Varrock.

Aubury is located south of Varrock's east bank, inside of his rune shop. Talk to Aubury, and he will give you some notes to deliver back to Wizard Sedridor. He will also offer the player a cup of tea, which will completely restore run energy if accepted.
Make your way back to the Wizards' Tower, and talk to Archmage Sedridor once more. He will give you back your air talisman and explain the basics of Runecraft.
Tip: Ask Archmage Sedridor to teleport you to the rune essence mine to complete an easy Lumbridge & Draynor diary task.
Congratulations, quest complete!
Talk to Thormac on the top floor of the Sorcerer's Tower south of Seers' Village. (What do you need assistance with? → So how would I go about catching them then? → Ok, I will do it then) (blr)

Go to Seers Village and speak to a Seer. (Wait until the seer is done checking himself in the mirror.) (Your friend Thormac sent me to speak to you.) Be sure not to skip this step, as the scorpion in Taverley Dungeon is not accessible without first speaking to the seer.
Scorpions can be caught in any order and there is no need to return between each catch.
Note: You will need a dusty key if you don't have 70 Agility, make sure to grab it before entering the dungeon.
Go into Taverley Dungeon, (South Taverley) and go to the poison spider area.

If you need a dusty key head south to the Black Knights' Base and kill the jailer. Use the key on the jail cell and talk to Velrak the explorer. He will give you the key. Alternatively, a dusty key spawns deep in Taverley Dungeon, near the lava eel fishing spot south of the blue dragon area.
Directly south of the level 80 Agility shortcut, search the old wall to enter a small room.
Use the scorpion cage on the Kharid Scorpion. If you try to pick it up, it will sting you instead.
Go to the Barbarian Outpost (a games necklace is helpful).
Go inside the fenced in area near the entrance to the agility course.
Go inside the building in the north-east corner of the area.
Use the scorpion cage on the Kharid Scorpion. If you try to pick it up, it will sting you instead.
Note: It is possible for the scorpion to be outside of the small room, in the Agility area, if someone has let it out.
Go to the [[Edgeville Monastery
Climb the eastern ladder and go to the east side of the floor.
Note: If the Monk stops you and says only members of the order may go upstairs, simply say that you want to join and you will be allowed to go upstairs.
Use the scorpion cage on the Kharid Scorpion. If you try to pick it up, it will sting you instead.
Return the full scorpion cage to Thormac.
Congratulations, quest complete!

Talk to Thormac on the top floor of the Sorcerer's Tower, just south-east of the Ranging Guild and south of Seers' Village. He'll tell you that his rare Kharid Scorpions have escaped and are currently running loose. He'll give you a Scorpion cage to catch the scorpions with and suggest you go talk to the Seers that live just to the north.
Speak with any Seer in Seers' Village. He will tell you that the first scorpion is in a secret room with nasty spiders nearby. This is the Taverley Dungeon.

Note: The secret room is only accessible once you have spoken to the seer about the location of the first scorpion. Once that is done, you can now catch the three scorpions in any order and may skip talking to the Seer again to find their locations.
left

Note: In the following section, low levelled players are highly recommended to use an anti-dragon shield when passing the blue dragons, as their dragonfire can inflict up to 50 damage, which the shield reduces by roughly 80%. If used in combination with an antifire potion, the player will gain full immunity. If you have not started Dragon Slayer I to obtain the shield, read the following sections for a more difficult strategy to avoid the dragonfire. The blue dragons may also be skipped if you have 80 Agility.

Make your way to the Taverley Dungeon. Once inside, you can skip the following steps if you have 70+ Agility, by either using the shortcut to the blue dragons (70 Agility) or the shortcut directly to the poison spiders (80 Agility).

If you cannot use the shortcuts, a dusty key is required to enter the section of the dungeon that the scorpion is located in. If you do not already have one, follow the track towards the Black Knights' Base and kill the jailer located in the eastern area of the base, who will drop a jail key. Use the jail key on the door of the cell containing Velrak the explorer. Speak to him; ask if there are any good places to explore, and when he asks you if you want to go further into the dungeon, say yes and he will give you a dusty key. Head to the blue dragons area.

Walk south of the blue dragons, west to pass the black demons, and north to the poison spiders. To the south of the two coffins, there's a small room with a false wall that you can search to open (see the map). If you are unable to open the door, you probably did not speak with the seer about the first scorpion.
Use the scorpion cage on the small scorpion inside this room to catch it (if you try to pick it up, it will sting you for 3 Hitpoints of damage).

Strategy without anti-dragon shield: When running past the blue dragons, ensure a baby blue dragon is fighting you at all times (they do not breathe dragonfire). The dungeon is single-combat, so the more dangerous blue dragons will not attack you while you are in combat. Avoid standing too close to adult dragons, and hop from baby to baby and draw their aggression when passing through. This strategy is not recommended for hardcore ironmen who are not confident they know what they are doing.

The second scorpion is on the of the Edgeville Monastery. To enter the you'll need to speak with Abbot Langley to join their guild (31 Prayer). You do not have to do this again if you have already done it.
Climb the south-east ladder in the Monastery. The scorpion will be either right at the top of the ladder, or in the bedroom directly north of the ladder. Use your cage on it to catch it.

The third scorpion is in the Barbarian Outpost Agility Course (requires completion of Alfred Grimhand's Barcrawl), found in the north eastern gated building. The scorpion will be wandering just inside the entrance. Use your cage on it to catch it.
Finally, bring the full scorpion cage to Thormac.
Congratulations, quest complete!

Talk to Alan again. (Of course!.)
Inspect the egg
Talk to [[King (Tal Teklan)
Talk to Acatzin in the inn (I can talk to the blacksmith!.)
Talk to the [[Blacksmith (Tal Teklan)
Repair the [[Whetstone (Tal Teklan)
Talk to the blacksmith again for Acatzin's axe, then repair it on the whetstone.
Return to Acatzin. Take a bowl from the table before you leave.
Fill the bowl with water at the fountain outside.
Talk to Nezketi at the temple directly south of the inn for an empty cup. (I can get you some tea!.)
Pick damiana leaves from the damiana directly outside of the south-eastern walls of Tal Teklan.
While you are there, head a bit further south-west and pick up the two planks.
Add the damiana leaves to the bowl of water.
Head to the Tal Teklan General Store just south of the bank.
Use the bowl on the oven to boil the damiana water.
Use the bowl on the empty cup, then return to Nezketi with the damiana tea.
Talk to Kauayotl, outside the eastern entrance of Tal Teklan. (I see. Well, maybe I can help out with that?)
Return to the blacksmith; pick up the hammer if you dropped it.
Search his workbench for 20 iron nails.
Pick up a saw at Arcuani's Archery Supplies just south of the blacksmith.
Repair the racing cart next to Kauayotl. (Yes.)
Talk to Kauayotl again.
Return to Tal Teok Temple and speak to any of King's men.
Large egg:
Search the eggs at the chicken farm directly south.
Defeat the large chicken and search the eggs again.
[[Dragon egg (Scrambled!)
Head to the bank for some combat equipment and dragonfire protection.
Enter the cave entrance to the Dragon Nest to the east (marked on the world map as [[File:Dungeon map link icon.png
Search the eggs again and head back outside.
Jaguar egg:
From the Dragon Nest, run eastwards until you reach a campsite.
Search the eggs and defeat the [[Black jaguar (Scrambled!)
Search the eggs again and return to Tal Teok.
Speak to each of King's men to initiate a cutscene.

Watch the final cutscene.

full.h: Humphrey Dumphrey Sat On A Wall

steps.t: Head to the temple of Tal Teok, just north of Tal Teklan. You will find a tourist named Alan, alongside his egg-shaped friend Humpy Plumpy, who has chosen to occupy the temple as a squatter. He will ask that you stay as a guest and insists he prepare a feast, and requests you to look after Wumty Scrumpty while he gathers the food.

As soon as he leaves however, gravity claims the life of Hampty and results in a great fall. Inspect Gumty on the ground, which prompts you to head back to Tal Teklan to look for help. Talking to any citizen there will direct you to King, the local bartender for The King's Inn.
Speak to King located in the inn about your predicament. She will tell you that she has to stay and man the bar, but has capable men who are up to the task. She will direct you to three people.

Acatzin is also in the inn. He will help you as soon as he gets his axe back from the blacksmith. Head south-west to the furnace and speak to the blacksmith, who will tell you that his whetstone has broken and needs repairing.

Take the hammer nearby and repair the whetstone. He will then give you Acatzin's axe (not knowing that it is his) and ask you to repair it instead. Repair the axe on the whetstone then return to Acatzin and he will be on his merry way to Tal Teok.
Before leaving, take the empty bowl on the table.

Nezketi is found at the temple directly south of the inn. In order to help you, he will need to be on top of his game - he will need tea made from damiana leaves. Agree to get his tea, and he will give you an empty cup.
Damiana can be found directly outside of the south-eastern walls of Tal Teklan. While you are there, head a bit further south-west and pick up the two planks.

Acquire a bowl of water; if you didn't take a bowl earlier, pick it up on a table in The King's Inn. A fountain is right outside to fill the bowl. Use the damiana leaves on the bowl of water, then head into the Tal Teklan General Store just south of the bank, and use the bowl on the oven to boil the damiana water. Finally, use the bowl of tea on the empty cup to finally create damiana tea.
Head back to the temple and talk to Nezketi, who you will automatically give the tea to. Freshly energised, he will depart for the temple immediately after.

From the temple, head directly east to the eastern entrance of Tal Teklan, where you will find Kauayotl with a damaged cart. In order to help you, he will first need to sort out his racing cart. Offer to help repair it, and he will tell you what you'll need:
Two planks - if you did not pick up two planks earlier, there are two spawns south of the city.
Nails - search the blacksmith's workbench for 20 iron nails.
Hammer - spawns on the table south-west of the workbench
Saw - spawns on a table in Arcuani's Archery Supplies just south of the blacksmith.
Return to Kauayotl, repair the damaged cart, and speak to him again to have him on his way to the temple.

Head back north to Tal Teok and speak to any of the three men. It quickly becomes apparent that all of King's men couldn't put Pumpty Lumpty together again, and that replacing him is the only option. However, the three argue over which type of egg is suitable: a large chicken's, a dragon's, or a... jaguar's. You will offer to get all three and have them pick a suitable one.

Head to the small chicken farm directly south of the Tal Teok temple in the north of Tal Teklan, and search the pile of eggs. A level-16 large chicken will attack; defeat it, then search the eggs again to obtain a large egg.

The entrance to the Dragon Nest is found to the south-east of Tal Teok temple, across the river. Once inside, make your way to the south-east and search the pile of eggs. A level-106 red dragon will attack. Players can safespot the dragon using the eggs; defeat it, then search the eggs again to obtain a dragon egg.

Head back outside, and run eastwards until you reach a campsite. Search the pile of eggs, and a level-88 black jaguar will attack; as it has routefinding capabilities, you will have to trick the jaguar by standing next to tropical tree and a fern to safespot it. After triumphing over the egglaying jaguar search the eggs again to obtain a jaguar egg.

Return to Tal Teok and speak to each of King's men, who will each paint the egg to resemble Rumpty Bumpty as best they can. Once all three eggs have been given, a cutscene will play in which the eggs are judged. The chicken egg is deemed too small to be Wumty Scrumpty, the dragon egg's innate heat is melting the paint, and the jaguar egg is deemed to be the best replacement for Mumpty Rumpty.

However, gravity is a cruel mistress and claims the lives of all the eggs, resulting in three additional great falls. With no options left, you and King's men must put Humphrey Dumphrey together again.

There are many pieces to reassemble, but players can hover over the puzzle piece icon to view the solution. When a piece is rotated in the correct orientation and placed in the correct location, it will stay in place indicating the correct placement.

Upon putting Scrumpty Lumpy back together again, a cutscene will play in which you thank King's men before they take their leave, and Alan returns none the wiser. As you head down to help him bring in the food, he reflects on his life, finally sure of himself and his place in the world. However, gravity is apparently out for blood, giving Alan a great fall.

Note: Players who wish to keep Alan's bones as a souvenir should ensure they do not have a bonecrusher or bonecrusher necklace on their person before fixing Bumpty Numpty, as the bonecrusher deems the player responsible for his death and will automatically crush his bones.
